short_description: Computes the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, from Pólya's integral for Xi in certified ball arithmetic, and proves that finite positivity tests on the heat trace cannot decide it; with hitting times, the reciprocal zeta function and Lee Yang theory.
description:
The Riemann Hypothesis can be restated as the positivity of a measure, the Thorin measure of a ratio of values of Riemann's Xi function. This book computes that measure from Pólya's integral for Xi, without primes or a list of zeros, in certified ball arithmetic, and asks what such computations can and cannot teach about the zeros.

A certified zero off the critical line would refute the hypothesis, but no finite computation can prove it. From the zeros verified up to height 3 × 10^12 the book certifies that the derivatives of the heat trace have the predicted signs up to order 1.16 × 10^25, and proves that such finite positivity tests cannot settle it: a perturbation of Xi with the same zeros below a large height, and zeros off the line above it, passes them. No proof of the hypothesis is claimed.

New results: the reciprocal Xi function at x to the power p is hyperbolically completely monotone exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi; at the basepoint one the Thorin density is certified smallest at the origin, so the shifted clock is a stable variable plus a generalized gamma convolution; between the basepoints one half and one the shifted clocks are almost generalized gamma convolutions, unconditionally; the clock of Pólya's Bessel function is the hitting time of an explicit diffusion; adjacent real zeros of a polynomial cannot meet under the backward heat flow before an explicit time; and the Pólya law lies within 2 × 10^-6 in total variation of the ferromagnetic laws of Lee and Yang, a distance that is zero exactly under the hypothesis.

An appendix lists the scripts and data files behind the tables and figures, which are in the book's repository https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh.

chapters.title: Introduction and foundations
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) as a positivity condition. For the completed zeta function $\xi$, put $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)$; the reciprocal $1/G$ is the clock. RH holds exactly when the clock is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC), whose Thorin measure is then the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. This is the Thorin condition. Its equivalent forms are sign conditions: $G'/G$ is a Stieltjes transform, the heat trace of the zeros is completely monotone, the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ is nonnegative at every resolution $\varepsilon>0$ (Lagarias's criterion), Weil's explicit formula functional is positive, and the clock is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM). The chapter introduces the Hadamard product, the Pólya kernel and density, van Dantzig pairs, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros (the Cauchy flow) and the sine squared lemma, which gives the Thorin density from the primes. It treats GGCs for computation: the Bondesson hierarchy, diagnostics of the Thorin condition and the sinh clock benchmark. It explains why computation can measure but not prove the Thorin condition.

#### From the literature

The Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); extended GGCs (Thorin 1978); the HCM characterization of GGC Laplace transforms (Bondesson 1992); Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); Pólya's integral for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926); van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968) and their link with RH (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024); the Bessel hitting time form of $\xi$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001, after Williams 1990); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

The chapter restates the rigidity and shifted clock theorems of Polson (2026), proves the sine squared lemma of Polson (2017) again, and adds one open question on positivity on a single line.

- [Rigidity of the clock, a GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rigidity_clock_ggc_iff_rh) (Proposition 1.2.1, page 12; proved): The clock, the reciprocal of the normalised completed zeta function in the variable $u=s^2$, is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, and then its Thorin measure is the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Shifted clock is a GGC to the right of every zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_ggc_right_of_every_zero) (Theorem 1.2.2, page 17; proved): To the right of every zero of the completed zeta function, in particular at every basepoint $\alpha\ge 1$, the shifted clock is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit positive Thorin density, and it is one exactly when $\alpha$ is at least the supremum of the real parts of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_line_positivity_exclusion_open) (Remark 1.2.4, page 18; open): It is not known, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, whether nonnegativity of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed zeta function on a single vertical line excludes zeros to the right of that line. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Riemann xi function, completed zeta function, Thorin condition, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, clock, rigidity theorem, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, heat trace, van Dantzig pair, Cauchy flow, sine squared lemma, Bondesson class, HCM, Lagarias criterion, sinh clock

chapters.title: Evaluating the Xi function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how to evaluate the Riemann xi function $\xi$ and its derivative at complex arguments, the raw material for computing the Thorin density at every resolution. The Pólya route applies the trapezoid rule to Pólya's integral $\Xi(\theta)=\int\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$. It needs neither primes nor zeros and is spectrally accurate because the Pólya kernel $\Phi$ is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/4$. The evaluator is two fixed polynomials in Arb ball arithmetic; below height 200 it gives about 60 correct digits and recovers the 79 zeros, with the count read from the argument principle. Cancellation costs about $0.341\,\theta$ digits at height $\theta$; tilting the contour into the strip reduces the loss to about $\delta\theta/\log 10$ digits and gives 25 digits of the Thorin density at height 5000. The chapter compares the route with the Riemann Siegel formula, the Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm and Turing's method, resolves the Lehmer pair near height 7005, reads the count $N(1000)=649$ from the Thorin mass, and ends with a worked computation from the theta series to the first zero. Ball radii certify rounding only, so the results are computed, not certified.

#### From the literature

Pólya's integral for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926); the exponentially convergent trapezoid rule (Trefethen and Weideman 2014); Arb ball arithmetic (Johansson 2017); the Riemann Siegel formula (Siegel 1932; Gabcke 1979); Gram points and Gram's law (Gram 1903), Rosser's rule (Rosser, Yohe and Schoenfeld 1969) and their failures (Brent 1979; Trudgian 2011); Backlund's count (Backlund 1918; Hutchinson 1925); Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011); the Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm (Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988); the Lehmer pair (Lehmer 1956); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

The tilted Pólya representation is new in the book. Digit counts, timings and zero counts are computed, with ball arithmetic certifying rounding only.

- [Tilted Pólya representation of xi and its derivative](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_representation_of_xi) (Proposition 2.1.1, page 34; proved): Moving the line of integration of Pólya's integral into the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel gives exact integral formulas for $\xi$ and $\xi'$ on a line at distance $\delta$ from the edge of the strip, with kernel bounds of order $\delta^{-5/2}$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann xi function, Pólya route, Polya route, Pólya kernel, trapezoid rule, spectral accuracy, tilted contour, ball arithmetic, Arb, Riemann Siegel formula, Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm, Gram points, Rosser's rule, Turing's method, Backlund's method, argument principle, zero counting, Lehmer pair, Thorin density, Thorin mass

chapters.title: The Thorin measure at finite resolution
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what finite computations of the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon$, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros of $\xi$, can establish about the Riemann Hypothesis. On the window below height 200, where the 79 zeros are known, it measures the distance from the computed Thorin measure to the discrete measure demanded by RH. Raw total variation is maximal, matched total variation sits at a numerical floor of about $3.7\times10^{-9}\varepsilon$, and cell distance, mass defect and heat trace error vanish linearly in the resolution $\varepsilon$. The chapter proves the first order mass defect, closed form signatures of an off line zero, a Littlewood identity, and a zero density identity that counts the zeros to the right of any line from the cumulative Thorin mass (at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, Backlund's count with the vertical side on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$). It shows that the sine squared lemma and Selberg's smoothed explicit formula give the Thorin density from the primes only at a cost exponential in $1/\varepsilon$, and explains why a finite computation can refute RH by certifying a zero off the line but cannot measure a distance to RH.

#### From the literature

Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); the argument principle count, the Riemann von Mangoldt formula and Littlewood's lemma (see Titchmarsh 1986); Backlund's method (Backlund 1918) and Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011); Selberg's smoothed explicit formula (Selberg 1946); Weil's positivity criterion (Weil 1952); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021). The sine squared lemma is an earlier result of Polson (2017); the canonical measure of $\log\xi$ that the sine squared decomposition uses and the square root law for a displaced zero are earlier results of Polson (2026).

#### New results

The propositions below are new in the book. The tables of distances, masses and counts at height 200 are computed, not certified.

- [Mass defect of the Thorin measure on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_first_order_defect) (Proposition 3.2.2, page 58; proved): When every zero up to height $\Theta$ lies on the critical line, the Thorin mass of the window $(0,\Theta^2]$ equals the zero count $N(\Theta)$ minus $(\varepsilon/\pi)\,\Xi'(\Theta)/\Xi(\Theta)$ up to a remainder of order $\varepsilon^2$. New in this book.
- [Signatures of an off line zero in the Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_zero_signatures) (Proposition 3.3.1, page 61; proved): The effect of an off line pair of zeros on the Thorin density is computed in closed form: a displacement that keeps the count has total variation $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2$ per displaced zero to leading order for $\delta<\varepsilon$, an omitted pair has total variation $\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, and a displaced zero has negative mass $\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, the last two for $\delta>\varepsilon$; the quadratic growth of the first is the square root law of Polson (2026). New in this book.
- [Littlewood identity for the cumulative Thorin mass](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#littlewood_identity_thorin_mass) (Proposition 3.4.1, page 66; proved): The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ is $\pi^{-1}$ times the derivative in $\varepsilon$ of the integral of $\log|\xi|$ along the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, which links the mass to the integral of $\log|\xi|$ on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Zero density identity from the Thorin mass](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_density_identity_thorin_mass) (Proposition 3.4.2, page 67; proved): The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ plus a short horizontal correction equals the zero count $N(T)$ minus twice the number of zeros to the right of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ it is Backlund's unconditional count of $N(T)$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Thorin density, Thorin mass, resolution, Poisson smoothing, Cauchy kernel, total variation, matched total variation, cell distance, mass defect, Richardson extrapolation, off line zero, square root law, Littlewood identity, zero density, argument principle, Backlund count, Turing's method, Selberg explicit formula, sine squared lemma, variogram, Weil criterion

chapters.title: Weak limits, hyperbolic complete monotonicity and a Bosch type theorem
chapters.summary:
Can closure of generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) under weak limits, or Bondesson's characterization of GGC Laplace transforms as hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) functions, settle the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) without locating zeros? For the reciprocal Xi function (the clock) the chapter recalls (Polson 2017) that the Cauchy flow of Thorin measures converges vaguely to the measure of the zeros on the critical line whether or not RH holds, so weak closure cannot reach RH, and shows that HCM of the clock is RH in other forms (Stieltjes and Pick function conditions, HCM of the de Bruijn Newman deformation at every positive time). An elasticity criterion for HCM functions transfers Bosch's method for powers of the half Cauchy law: the clock composed with x^p is HCM exactly when |p| is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, with RH the extreme case, and unconditionally for |p| within about 10^-13 of one, by the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12. Further results: the Thorin density of this family, a natural boundary argument with the Dedekind eta function, a first gap condition for the Mellin variable W (under RH and further hypotheses), and open questions.

#### From the literature

Closure of generalized gamma convolutions under convergence in law (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Bondesson's theorem that a Laplace transform is a GGC transform if and only if it is HCM (Bondesson 1992; James, Roynette and Yor 2008); Bondesson's representation of HCM functions (Bondesson 1992); Bosch's theorem on powers of the half Cauchy law (Bosch 2015); the proof of Bondesson's conjecture on stable densities (Bosch and Simon 2016); Lagarias's criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999); the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020), at most 0.22 (Polymath 2019) and at most 0.2 (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Lamperti's stable ratio density (Lamperti 1958); the Mellin representation of xi (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Pólya's gap theorem (Pólya 1923, 1929).

#### New results

- [RH as a weak limit criterion for generalized gamma convolutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_clock_is_weak_limit_of_ggc_transforms) (Corollary 4.1.2, page 77; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal Xi function is the pointwise limit of Laplace transforms of generalized gamma convolutions on a set of points with an accumulation point in the positive half line. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal Xi function is HCM if and only if RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_rh) (Corollary 4.1.3, page 80; proved): The reciprocal Xi function with basepoint alpha at least one is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) unconditionally, and with basepoint one half (the clock) it is HCM if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds; the equivalence for the clock is noted in versions 21 and 23 of Polson's arXiv paper 1708.02653, and both parts follow from Polson (2026) by Bondesson's theorem. New in this book.
- [Deformed reciprocal Xi function is HCM exactly for t at least Lambda](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deformed_reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_time_at_least_lambda) (Corollary 4.2.5, page 88; proved): The reciprocal Xi function deformed by the de Bruijn Newman heat flow to time t is HCM exactly when t is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, so RH is equivalent to HCM for every positive t. New in this book.
- [Question: for which beta is the density of W^beta HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_powers_of_mellin_variable_w) (Question 4.2.7, page 89; open): The book asks for which powers beta the density of W to the power beta is HCM, where W is the positive variable with Mellin transform Xi(0)/Xi(z). chapters.title: The heat trace, the arithmetic and the limits of finite information
chapters.summary:
How much of the Thorin condition on the reciprocal Xi function (RH) follows from sign conditions on the heat trace W(t), the sum of exp(-a_j t) over the zeros of the Riemann xi function, and what can finite information not decide? Using only the verification of RH to a finite height (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and Weil's explicit formula for the primes, the chapter proves that W is positive and decreasing (Polson 2026), so the clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable; sketches the proof (Polson 2017) that the derivatives of W alternate in sign up to order 10^17; and proves, by a window theorem, that they do so up to order 1.16 times 10^25 (positivity of the Williamson measures) and that W is completely monotone on (0, 1.29]. Positive semidefinite Hankel matrices of the derivatives at one time are equivalent to RH, the numbers of negative eigenvalues of Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments tend to the number of quadruples of zeros off the critical line, and RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of a Gaussian smoothing of the zeros. A perturbation of xi with four off line zeros passes finite heat trace tests, and a certified zero of a Mellin transform of the Pólya density closes the Bernstein Pick route. The chapter also defines the Thorin functional from the primes and compares zero spacings with GUE statistics.

#### From the literature

Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); self decomposability of laws with a nonincreasing W(t) in the Lévy density W(t)/t (Sato 1999) and unimodality (Yamazato 1978); Mase's theorem on indecomposable factors (Mase 1975) and Linnik's class I_0 (Linnik 1964); Williamson's theorem on k monotone functions (Williamson 1956); Hermite's count of nonreal roots by Hankel forms (Hermite 1856), with Grommer (1914), Chebotarev (1928) and Baricz and Štampach (2018); Hutchinson's early verification of zeros (Hutchinson 1925); the explicit Riemann von Mangoldt formula (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); solutions of the van Dantzig problem (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024); pair correlation (Montgomery 1973) and spacings (Odlyzko 1987); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Guth and Maynard 2026).

#### New results

- [The clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, unconditionally](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_infinitely_divisible_and_self_decomposable) (Theorem 5.1.1, page 116; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 1000, the heat trace is positive and decreasing, so the clock is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law with Lévy density W(t)/t, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Hankel positivity of the heat trace at one time is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_positivity_at_one_time_iff_rh) (Theorem 5.1.2, page 119; proved): At any single time t, positive semidefiniteness of the two Hankel matrices of derivatives of the heat trace, equivalently of Weil's quadratic form on the span of r^m exp(-r^2 t/2), is equivalent to RH. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Positive definite Hankel blocks of the heat trace up to size 3 x 10^7](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_hankel_blocks_positive_definite_to_size_3e7) (Theorem 5.1.3, page 120; proved): If every zero of xi below height 20000 N (1 + log N)^(1/2) lies on the critical line, the leading N by N Hankel blocks of the derivatives of the heat trace are positive definite at every time, and the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12 gives this unconditionally for every N up to 3 times 10^7. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 10^17](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e17) (Theorem 5.1.4, page 120; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 10^12, the derivatives of the heat trace alternate in sign, (-1)^k W^(k)(t) > 0, for every t > 0 and every order k up to 10^17. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments count the zeros off the critical line (eigenvalue form of the Grommer and Chebotarev criterion)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_inertia_counts_zeros_off_critical_line) (Theorem 5.1.5, page 122; proved): In an eigenvalue form of the classical determinant criterion of Grommer (1914) and Chebotarev (1928), the numbers of negative eigenvalues of the Hankel matrices of the Stieltjes moments of the heat trace are nondecreasing in the matrix size and tend to the number of distinct zeros of xi to the right of the critical line in the upper half plane, so RH holds if and only if they are all zero. New in this book.
- [Heat trace completely monotone on (0, 1.29]; every order up to t = 0.019](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_completely_monotone_near_origin) (Theorem 5.1.7, page 125; proved): Every derivative of the heat trace of order at least one alternates in sign for t up to 0.019 using no information on the zeros, and with the verification of RH below height 10^12 the heat trace is completely monotone on (0, 1.29], with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Heat trace derivative along a ray is the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_along_ray_is_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros) (Proposition 5.1.8, page 130; proved): For u at least 2 and k equal to u^2 t, not necessarily an integer, the k th derivative of the heat trace (defined by its sum over the zeros), divided by an explicit factor, equals the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution 1/(2 sqrt t) up to an explicit relative error on each zero within u/2 of u and an explicit remainder, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros_nonnegative) (Proposition 5.1.9, page 131; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros of xi, a sum of Gaussian bumps in complexified ordinates, is nonnegative for every real centre and every resolution. New in this book.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e25) (Theorem 5.1.10, page 136; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Four off line zeros that pass the finite heat trace tests](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_perturbation_passing_finite_heat_trace_tests) (Theorem 5.2.1, page 137; proved): Moving a close pair of zeros of xi on the critical line to four zeros at distance one quarter off the line gives an even entire function whose heat trace still passes the finite tests (infinite divisibility, self decomposability, log convexity, and at large heights positive Hankel blocks and derivative signs up to order 10^17). First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Certified zero of a Mellin transform closes the Bernstein Pick route to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bernstein_pick_route_closed_by_certified_zero) (Theorem 5.2.2, page 143; proved): A certified simple zero of the meromorphically continued Mellin transform M of the Pólya density near -8.494 + 2.938i gives the canonical interpolant of the moment ratios a nonreal pole, so no Bernstein interpolant is a complete Bernstein function and the Bernstein Pick route to RH is closed. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, heat trace, Thorin measure, Thorin condition, reciprocal Xi function, clock, infinitely divisible, self decomposable, completely monotone, Williamson measure, k monotone, Hankel matrix, Stieltjes moments, Weil explicit formula, Gaussian smoothing of the zeros, van Dantzig pair, Pólya density, verification of RH, Bernstein Pick route, spacing of zeros, GUE, cell distance

chapters.title: The reciprocal zeta function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the zeros, the primes and the gamma factor of the Riemann zeta function assemble into a Thorin measure, that is, whether the reciprocal zeta function, in the clock variable, is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) or at least infinitely divisible. From the Dirichlet series and Euler product it computes Thorin type measures of an Euler factor and, under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, the signed measure $dM$ with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, and from the Weierstrass product that of the gamma factor. The Lai and Vere-Jones identity gives the Vere-Jones representation by hyperbolic secants and sawtooth measures, and an explicit canonical function (heat trace) that yields a criterion for RH. The sine squared lemma and the Meixner law show that the reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt, and the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, whose infinite divisibility follows from Polson (2026), is a GGC exactly when RH holds.

#### From the literature

- the Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- the hyperbolic secant law as a Brownian exit time and a GGC, and its gamma powers $C_t$ with Laplace transform $(\cosh\sqrt{2\lambda})^{-t}$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- the Meixner hypergeometric law and the completeness problem for dilates of the hyperbolic secant (Lai and Vere-Jones 1979)
- the Riemann von Mangoldt formula (see Titchmarsh 1986) and the explicit formula (Weil 1952), in its heat trace form (Polson 2026)
- the local Riemann Hypothesis for Mellin transforms of even Hermite functions (Bump, Choi, Kurlberg and Vaaler 2000), rederived here with no priority claimed, and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of $\Xi$ (Kuznetsov 2008; Romik 2021)
- Williamson's theorem on $n$ monotone functions (Williamson 1956)
- the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and a bound for the zero count (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- infinite divisibility and self decomposability of the reciprocal Xi function (Polson 2026)

#### New results

The results below first appeared in Part IX of Polson (2026), five of them corrected or sharpened here; the two sine squared lemmas are from Polson (2017).

- [Thorin type density of an Euler factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#euler_factor_thorin_type_density) (Proposition 6.1.2, page 159; proved): The Euler factor $1-qe^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ is zero free on the cut plane and has an explicit Thorin type density, a cosine series of both signs. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a Möbius sum of hyperbolic secants)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lai_vere_jones_identity) (Proposition 6.1.3, page 160; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals a Möbius weighted sum of the dilates $\operatorname{sech}(mx)$ of the hyperbolic secant, which expands the Dirichlet series of the reciprocal zeta function in hyperbolic secants; the book names it after Lai and Vere-Jones, who posed the completeness of these dilates as an open problem. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of the reciprocal zeta function by hyperbolic secants](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_reciprocal_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.5, page 160; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ equals $1$ plus an explicit Möbius weighted series of hyperbolic secants $\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt s\log N)$, each the Laplace transform of a Brownian exit time and a GGC with atomic Thorin measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a sum of logarithms with Dirichlet eta weights)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_as_eta_weighted_sum_of_log_blocks) (Proposition 6.1.6, page 161; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals $\sum_{m\ge1}d_m\log(1+e^{-mx})$ with weights $d_m$ bounded by $1$ whose Dirichlet series is $1/\eta(1+v)$ for Dirichlet's eta function $\eta$, the logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth Thorin measure of a Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_thorin_measure_of_vere_jones_block) (Lemma 6.1.7, page 161; proved): The function $2/(1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s})$ has the signed Thorin type measure formed by unit atoms at the squares of the odd multiples of $\pi/\lambda$ minus the density $\lambda/(4\pi\sqrt t)$, a sawtooth measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of log zeta by sawtooth blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_log_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.8, page 162; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $\log\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is an explicit absolutely convergent series of the blocks $\log(1+N^{-\sqrt s})$ with weights from Dirichlet's eta function, and its derivative is a sum of Stieltjes transforms with poles on sawtooth lattices. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin type measure of the normalised reciprocal zeta function under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_normalised_reciprocal_zeta_under_rh) (Theorem 6.1.10, page 163; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the normalised reciprocal zeta function has the signed Thorin type measure $dM$, unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros plus the density of the gamma factor, with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, so it is not a GGC even under RH. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Canonical function of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, prime and zero forms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#canonical_function_normalised_reciprocal_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.11, page 164; proved): With no hypothesis, $-\varphi'/\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of the canonical function $w(x)=e^{x/4}-P(x)$, explicit in the primes, which by the arithmetic form of the heat trace (Weil's explicit formula; Polson 2026, Theorem 4.4) equals the heat trace over the zeros minus the heat trace of their smooth count. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Theta function series for the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_series_for_canonical_function_reciprocal_zeta) (Proposition 6.1.13, page 166; proved): The canonical function $w$ equals $e^{x/4}$ plus an absolutely convergent series of Jacobi theta functions, one for each prime power, with the weights $B_N$ of the Vere-Jones representation. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth expansion of the argument function after Gaussian averaging, under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_expansion_argument_function_gaussian_average) (Corollary 6.1.14, page 167; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the Gaussian average of the argument function $S$ equals $(e^{x/4}-1)/x$ plus the $B_N$ weighted Gaussian averages of sawtooth functions, which makes the sawtooth expansion of $S$ rigorous after Gaussian averaging. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Criterion for RH from the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_criterion_from_canonical_function) (Theorem 6.1.15, page 167; proved): RH is equivalent to the function $w$, explicit in the primes, being the Laplace transform of a real signed measure $m$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $\int|m|(dt)/(1+t)<\infty$, and the measure is then $dM$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin measure of the gamma factor as a renormalised product of Poisson kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_the_gamma_factor) (Theorem 6.2.1, page 170; proved): The gamma factor $\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ is a renormalised infinite product with signed Thorin type measure $-\theta'(\sqrt t)/(2\pi\sqrt t)\,dt$, a series of Poisson kernels of widths $2n+\frac12$ with flat compensators. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Closed form heat trace over the zeros and formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_closed_form_and_formal_thorin_measure_of_reciprocal_xi) (Theorem 6.2.3, page 172; proved): The heat trace $W(x)$ over the zeros has an explicit absolutely convergent closed form, the polar term, a theta series over prime powers and complementary error functions over the poles of the gamma factor, equivalently the Laplace transform of a formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sine squared lemma (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_polson_2017) (Lemma 6.2.4, page 174; proved): A Lévy representation of $\log f$ gives, through the kernel $2\sin^2$, a Lévy representation in the variable $s^2/2$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+s)$, by a linear positivity preserving map of the Lévy measure. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Sine squared lemma in the variable s = u squared (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_clock_variable) (Lemma 6.2.5, page 174; proved): In the variable $s=u^2$ a Lévy measure $\tilde\mu$ of $\log f$ gives the Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\int2\sin^2(\frac{x\sqrt t}2)\tilde\mu(dx)$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(0)/f(\sqrt s)$, so a positive $\tilde\mu$ gives a GGC; this restates Lemma 1 of Polson (2017) with a proof by subordination. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Reciprocal zeta to the right of the line Re z = 1 is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_right_of_line_one_tilted_ggc) (Proposition 6.2.6, page 175; proved): For $\beta>1$ the function $\zeta(\beta)/\zeta(\beta+\sqrt s)$ times the tilt $e^{\sqrt s\,\zeta'(\beta)/\zeta(\beta)}$ is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta}\,2\sin^2(\frac{\sqrt t\log n}2)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positive Thorin density of a shifted Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_vere_jones_block_positive_thorin_density) (Proposition 6.2.7, page 176; proved): After a shift of the basepoint by $\alpha>0$ and an explicit stable tilt, the reciprocal of the block $1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ has a positive Poisson kernel Thorin density, which tends to the lattice of atoms of the sawtooth measure as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Divergence of the cosine Lévy series of the Vere-Jones blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_levy_series_of_vere_jones_blocks_diverges) (Proposition 6.2.9, page 177; proved): The cosine Lévy forms of the sawtooth blocks cannot be summed with the weights $B_N$, because for every $x>0$ the series $\sum_NB_NK_{U_{\log N}}(x)$ diverges. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The Meixner density of the gamma factor is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#meixner_density_not_polya_frequency_function) (Proposition 6.2.10, page 178; proved): The Meixner density $|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ of the gamma factor, with characteristic function $\operatorname{sech}(v)^{1/2}$, is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, because by Schoenberg's theorem the reciprocal $\cosh(v)^{1/2}$ of its characteristic function would have to be entire. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Bernstein function of the gamma factor: theta derivative and Meixner score](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_factor_bernstein_function_and_meixner_score) (Proposition 6.2.11, page 179; proved): The function $\psi(\frac14+\frac\lambda2)-\psi(\frac14)$ is a Bernstein function whose boundary values on the imaginary axis have real part $2(\theta'(\tau)-\theta'(0))$ and imaginary part the Meixner score $-\frac{d}{d\tau}\log p(\tau)$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_reciprocal_gamma_factor_is_ggc) (Theorem 6.2.12, page 180; proved): After the stable tilt $e^{-c\sqrt s}$ with $c=\zeta'(\frac12)/\zeta(\frac12)$, the reciprocal of the gamma factor is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $(\theta'(\sqrt t)-\theta'(0))/(2\pi\sqrt t)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Factorisation of the Pólya autocorrelation through the Meixner law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_autocorrelation_meixner_factorisation) (Proposition 6.2.14, page 183; proved): The autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel is a fourth order differential operator applied to the Fourier transform of $p|\zeta|^2$ on the critical line, formally the Meixner characteristic function convolved with a positive measure on the lattice $\{\log(m/n)\}$, and the lattice sum diverges because of the pole of $\zeta$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Splitting of the canonical function of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, and GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_reciprocal_xi_infinitely_divisible_ggc_iff_rh) (Theorem 6.2.15, page 185; proved): With no hypothesis the canonical function $W(x)+c/(2\sqrt{\pi x})$ of the floor $e^{-c\sqrt s}\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the sum of the function $w$, explicit in the primes and proved positive with certified interval enclosures and the verification of RH to height $50$, and a completely monotone archimedean part, which reproves that the floor is infinitely divisible (this also follows from Theorem A of Polson 2026); the floor is a GGC if and only if RH holds. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Derivative signs of the canonical function of the floor to order ten billion, a separate proof (Williamson measures)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_canonical_function_derivative_signs_to_order_1e10) (Theorem 6.2.17, page 187; proved): The canonical function $k$ of the floor satisfies $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for all $y>0$ and every $n\le10^{10}$, proved by a two range argument from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, a bound for the zero count and one certified interval enclosure, which gives positive Williamson measures; the signs to order $10^{17}$ follow from Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), and to order $1.16\times10^{25}$ from the book's heat trace estimates. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

#### Key terms

reciprocal zeta function, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, infinite divisibility, canonical function, heat trace, Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Lai and Vere-Jones identity, hyperbolic secant, sawtooth measure, Meixner Pollaczek polynomials, local Riemann Hypothesis, sine squared lemma, stable tilt, floor of the reciprocal Xi function

chapters.title: Infinite divisibility and truncations of the reciprocal zeta function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks where the normalised reciprocal zeta function $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s))$ sits among infinitely divisible laws, and how far truncations of the Biane Pitman Yor lattice go towards the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Unconditionally, and certified in interval arithmetic, it proves that the canonical function $w$ is positive, so that $\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law with Lévy density $w(x)/x$, which is not self decomposable, not in the Bondesson class and not a generalized gamma convolution (GGC). It reads the Vere-Jones weights as necklace polynomials, extends the canonical function across the critical strip, and states the Laguerre Pólya class and the Lee and Yang property in Thorin measure terms. For simple zeros $\rho$, zeros of the truncated lattice transforms converge to $\rho/2$ at rate $1/n$: the one sided Conjecture T is false, while the symmetrised Conjecture S is proved above explicit heights for $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ and only checked numerically below them. It also proves Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone and reads the de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs.

#### From the literature

Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992), closed under independent products (Bondesson 2015); unimodality of self decomposable laws (Yamazato 1978); Selberg's central limit theorem for $S(t)$ (Selberg 1946); verification of RH to height 50 (Backlund 1918) and $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); simplicity of the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter 1986); an explicit Riemann von Mangoldt bound (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); necklace polynomials (Metropolis and Rota 1983); Pólya's theory of real zeros (Pólya 1926), Cardon's theorems (Cardon 2004, 2005), zeros of $\xi(s+a)+\xi(s-a)$ for $a\ge\frac12$ (Lagarias 2005), the Lee and Yang theorem (Lee and Yang 1952), Newman's characterization of Lee and Yang spins (Newman 1974); the Biane Pitman Yor identity (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001; Williams 1990); Weil's criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000); the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976; Rodgers and Tao 2020; Polymath 2019; Platt and Trudgian 2021).

Most results below first appeared in Part IX of Polson (2026); uncertified numerical checks are not catalogued.

First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

chapters.title: Probability, hitting times and other criteria
chapters.summary:
What else does the Pólya density compute about the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? The clock $1/G$ of Riemann's xi function is the Laplace transform of a random variable $T$, self decomposable with no hypothesis on the zeros and a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when RH holds, and the Pólya route computes its law with no zero as input. The chapter studies this clock variable (hazard rate, Kent approximants, Monte Carlo through Williams' representation), proves that it is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level, and computes a curved Brownian boundary for it from the Volterra equation. It computes the Keiper Li coefficients, reads Li's criterion as positivity of the Thorin functional, and follows the de Bruijn Newman flow to the collisions of zeros, with a Hankel test and collision time bounds in terms of Laguerre's quantity suggested by Biane's free convolution with a semicircle law. It then evaluates the Dedekind eta kernel, Dirichlet $L$ functions and Ramanujan's $\Delta$, recovers zeros by nonnegative deconvolution, and treats Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$, for which the Thorin programme holds as theorems. No proof of RH is claimed.

#### From the literature

- Kent's eigenvalue expansion of hitting times (Kent 1980) and Krein's inverse spectral theory (Dym and McKean 1976).
- Williams' Bessel hitting time representation of $\xi$ (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Talbot inversion (Talbot 1979).
- Tangent approximation and inverse problem for first passage boundaries (Roberts and Shortland 1995; Ekström and Janson 2016).
- Li's criterion (Li 1997), Keiper's coefficients (Keiper 1992), Bombieri and Lagarias (1999), Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999).
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), Lehmer pair bounds (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994).
- Free convolution with a semicircle law (Biane 1997); Pólya's Bessel function (Pólya 1926); Biane's dictionary of hitting times and spectral measures, with corrected constants, and the Liouville operator of the zeros, going back to Titchmarsh (Biane 2009); Hecke's converse theorem (Hecke 1936).
- Generalised gamma convolutions and the Bondesson class (Bondesson 1992).

#### New results

Tables of computed values are numerical.

- [The clock is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_not_first_passage_time_to_random_level) (Proposition 8.2.1, page 252; proved): The clock variable of the Riemann xi function is not, for any constant drift and any independent random level, the first passage time of Brownian motion with that drift to that level, and the proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Keiper Li coefficients as values of the Thorin functional](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#keiper_li_coefficients_as_thorin_functional) (Proposition 8.3.1, page 261; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, each Keiper Li coefficient is the Thorin functional of the zeros paired with an explicit rational function that is nonnegative on the positive axis, so Li's criterion is nonnegativity of that functional on the cone spanned by these functions. New in this book.
- [Critical point lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_critical_point_collision_bound) (Theorem 8.4.6, page 278; proved): While all zeros stay real and simple, a gap between two zeros of a real polynomial cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over Laguerre's quantity at the critical point of the gap, and z squared minus a squared attains the bound. New in this book.
- [Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_biane_form_collision_bound) (Theorem 8.4.8, page 279; proved): While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre's quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared. New in this book.
- [Local lower bound for the closing of a gap with a correction from the nonreal zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_local_bound_nonreal_zeros) (Theorem 8.4.11, page 281; proved): For the minimum m of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros, the upper right Dini derivative is at most one plus an explicit correction, computed from the nonreal zeros, times m squared, which bounds the time at which the gap closes from below. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the closing of a gap from the quantity delta, with no knowledge of the nonreal zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_delta_collision_bound) (Corollary 8.4.12, page 282; proved): A quantity delta computed from the function and its first four derivatives at the minimiser of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros controls the growth of that minimum under the backward heat flow, and when delta stays at most zero until the collision the gap cannot close before Biane's time, one over the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity, even when nonreal zeros are present. New in this book.
- [Upper bound (deadline) for the closing time of a gap between real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_collision_deadline) (Theorem 8.4.13, page 282; proved): If the share Q of the other zeros and the sum W over the nonreal zeros stay below constants rho and W bar for which 3 rho plus the square root of 9 rho squared plus 6 W bar is less than the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between two real zeros, the gap closes, by a collision of one of its bounding zeros with another zero, no later than an explicit logarithmic time. New in this book.
- [Deadline for the closing of a gap in terms of the quantity kappa](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_collision_deadline_kappa_form) (Corollary 8.4.14, page 283; proved): The deadline for the closing of a gap holds with six times the bound on W replaced by the largest negative part of a quantity kappa, computed from the function at the minimiser and the two zeros bounding the gap, and this form is never weaker. New in this book.
- [Control of the nonreal zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function at negative times](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#nonreal_zeros_control_along_backward_heat_flow) (Problem 8.1, page 286; open): No bound is known, computed from the de Bruijn Newman function at time zero, for how far its nonreal zeros travel at negative times or how close to a gap between real zeros they come, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about that function. New in this book.
- [Max representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_representation_of_ramanujan_delta_l_function) (Theorem 8.5.2, page 296; proved): The completed L function of Ramanujan's cusp form Delta is the expectation of an incomplete gamma function at the random point 2 pi M*, where M* is a maximum of independent exponential variables, a representation with no signs. New in this book.
- [Gamma mixture and mixed Poisson forms of L values of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_mixture_and_mixed_poisson_forms_of_delta_l_values) (Corollary 8.5.3, page 297; proved): For real s above minus 11/2 the L value of Ramanujan's Delta is the probability that a gamma variable exceeds 2 pi M*, and at the points s equal to k minus 11/2 it is a mixed Poisson probability. New in this book.
- [L values of Delta and chi12 as infinitely divisible probabilities](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#delta_and_chi12_l_values_as_infinitely_divisible_probabilities) (Proposition 8.5.7, page 303; proved): By Kristiansen's theorem on Gamma(2) mixtures and the theorem of Goldie and Steutel on exponential mixtures, the L values of Ramanujan's Delta at real s between minus 11/2 and minus 7/2 and of the character chi12 at real s between 0 and 4 are probabilities that an infinitely divisible variable exceeds one. New in this book.
- [Laplace transform of the maximum M1 of exponentials in closed form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m1_closed_form) (Proposition 8.5.8, page 304; proved): The Laplace transform of the maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is an explicit ratio of a sine and a cosine, equal to an infinite product over the numbers b_n = pi (n squared minus 1)/12. New in this book.
- [Rényi type decomposition of the maximum M1 of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#renyi_type_decomposition_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Corollary 8.5.9, page 305; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is a sum of independent exponential variables whose rates are b_{6k-1} or b_{6k+1} with explicit probabilities p_k that decrease to one half. New in this book.
- [Lévy density and Bondesson function of the maximum M1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_density_and_bondesson_function_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Proposition 8.5.11, page 306; proved): The Lévy density of the maximum M1 has an explicit theta function form with stated behaviour at zero and infinity, and its Bondesson function N_1 is nonnegative and grows like a constant times the square root of z. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of M1 as a difference of two GGC Thorin measures](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_m1_difference_of_two_ggc_thorin_measures) (Theorem 8.5.12, page 307; proved): The maximum M1 plus an independent GGC Z has the law of a second GGC S, so the signed Thorin measure of M1 is the difference of two positive measures with unit atoms. New in this book.
- [Certified zeros of the Laplace transform of the maximum M* of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_zeros_of_laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m_star) (Proposition 8.5.13, page 309; proved): Certified in ball arithmetic: the Laplace transform of M* changes sign in each of 25 gaps between its poles, and has exactly one zero near each of ten nonreal points, so it has zeros off the real axis. New in this book.
- [The maximum M* of exponentials is not in the Bondesson class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_of_exponentials_m_star_not_in_bondesson_class) (Corollary 8.5.14, page 310; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n is not in the Bondesson class and so is not a GGC, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [Open question on infinite divisibility of maxima of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_infinite_divisibility_of_maxima_of_exponentials) (Question 8.5.15, page 311; open): Is every maximum of independent exponential variables infinitely divisible, and in particular is the maximum M* with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n? New in this book.
- [Open question on real zeros of cosh kernels with exponential multipliers](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_real_zeros_of_cosh_kernel_with_exponential_multiplier) (Question 8.5.16, page 315; open): For which parameters does the Fourier transform of the kernel exp(-a cosh u) times an exponential multiplier have only real zeros, a form shared by the kernels of Ramanujan's Delta, chi12 and the conductor 11 curve? New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_of_imaginary_quadratic_field) (Theorem 8.5.17, page 318; proved): The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the two sided Laplace transform of an even doubly exponentially decaying kernel, which is positive exactly when a one variable function is positive on a finite interval, in particular for the discriminants minus 3, minus 4, minus 7 and minus 8. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field takes negative values when 2 and 3 are inert](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_takes_negative_values_when_two_and_three_inert) (Theorem 8.5.18, page 320; proved): For every negative fundamental discriminant d congruent to 5 modulo 24 the Pólya kernel of Q(sqrt d) takes negative values, by an explicit evaluation of a finite sum with a bounded tail, and there are infinitely many such d. New in this book.
- [Open question on the density of positive Pólya kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_density_of_positive_polya_kernels_imaginary_quadratic) (Question 8.5.19, page 322; open): Does the proportion of imaginary quadratic fields with a positive Pólya kernel tend to a limit, is the limit positive, and is the kernel positive for infinitely many fields in which 2 and 3 split? New in this book.
- [Open question on positivity criteria for real quadratic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_positivity_criterion_polya_kernel_real_quadratic) (Question 8.5.20, page 322; open): Is there a criterion for positivity of the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function of a real quadratic field or a field of higher degree that is as simple as the one for imaginary quadratic fields? New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the Dirichlet beta function at basepoints from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Proposition 8.5.23, page 326; proved): The logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function at every basepoint alpha at least one has a Lévy form whose signed Lévy measure is an explicit positive gamma density plus prime power atoms of both signs. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function from basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Proposition 8.5.24, page 328; proved): For every basepoint alpha at least one the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a GGC with a positive explicit Thorin density, and, by Lagarias's criterion, GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the positivity of that density at every alpha above one half. New in this book.
- [Termwise positivity thresholds for the Dirichlet beta function and chi12](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#termwise_positivity_thresholds_dirichlet_beta_and_chi12) (Proposition 8.5.25, page 329; proved): Bounding the prime weights by their absolute values gives a positive Thorin density exactly for basepoints above 2.2823106368 for the Dirichlet beta function and above 1.8348743295 for chi12, thresholds located by bisection with certified signs. New in this book.
- [No bound from the sizes of the prime weights beats the absolute values](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_bound_from_prime_weight_sizes_beats_absolute_values_kronecker) (Proposition 8.5.26, page 330; proved): By Kronecker's theorem no lower bound for the real part of L'/L of the Dirichlet beta function better than minus the sum of the absolute weights holds at all large heights, and the height from which the termwise bound works grows like e to the power 2/(alpha minus 1). New in this book.
- [Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function as a difference over the Gaussian field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_dirichlet_beta_as_difference_over_gaussian_field) (Proposition 8.5.27, page 332; proved): On every vertical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is the difference of the Thorin densities of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) and of Riemann's xi function, and the canonical measures subtract in the same way. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and domination of Thorin densities over Q(i)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_gaussian_field_thorin_density_dominates_xi) (Corollary 8.5.28, page 332; conditional on Part (iii) assumes the Riemann hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function; parts (i) and (ii) hold without any hypothesis): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the Thorin density of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) dominating that of Riemann's xi at every basepoint, and for alpha at least one the GGC of Q(i) is the sum of independent GGCs for xi and for the Dirichlet beta function. New in this book.
- [Open question on a coupling construction over the Gaussian primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_coupling_construction_over_gaussian_primes) (Question 8.5.29, page 333; open): Is there a construction of the GGC attached to Q(i) from the Gaussian primes themselves that persists below the basepoint one? New in this book.
- [Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function as an argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_of_dirichlet_beta_as_argument_of_completed_function) (Proposition 8.5.30, page 333; proved): On a vertical line the cumulative Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function is the argument of the completed function divided by pi, with an asymptotic expansion that becomes the zero counting formula at the centre and a limit that counts the zeros on the critical line. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and monotonicity of the argument of the completed function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_argument_of_completed_function_nondecreasing) (Corollary 8.5.31, page 335; proved): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function being nondecreasing on every line to the right of the centre, and without any hypothesis it can fall only in short windows around zeros off the line, none below height 2.5 times 10^7 by Platt's verification. New in this book.
- [The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a gamma mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_kernel_of_dirichlet_beta_not_a_gamma_mixture) (Proposition 8.5.32, page 336; proved): The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of any shape, and the theta function eta(ix) cubed is not completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Open question on a reciprocal side representation from the eta product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_reciprocal_side_representation_from_eta_product) (Question 8.5.33, page 337; open): Can the complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the eta cube theta function, and of the reciprocal eta product for chi12, be turned into a positive representation on the reciprocal side in the spirit of Thorin? New in this book.
- [Laplace transform of Bessel hitting times with curvature](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_bessel_hitting_times_with_curvature) (Proposition 8.7.6, page 348; proved): The hitting time of radius a by the radial Brownian motion on the three dimensional space form of curvature kappa has an explicit Laplace transform, is a GGC with equally spaced Thorin atoms shifted by minus kappa/2, and is an exponential tilt of the flat case. The flat case is classical (Ciesielski and Taylor 1962), and for kappa < 0 the process is the Bessel process of dimension three with drift (Salminen and Vallois 2007), the norm of a three dimensional Brownian motion with drift, where the formula also follows from the Cameron Martin formula; the formula for the whole family, its Thorin measure and its reading as an exponential tilt are the book's. New in this book.
- [Exact quantisation rule for the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_quantisation_rule_for_zeros_of_polya_bessel_function) (Proposition 8.7.8, page 352; proved): The positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi) are exactly the solutions of an explicit phase equation, so their counting function is the integer part of a smooth function with an explicit asymptotic expansion. New in this book.
- [Index side Thorin measure of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#index_side_thorin_measure_of_polya_bessel_function) (Theorem 8.7.9, page 355; proved): For Pólya's Bessel function the reciprocal K_0(2 pi)/K_{sqrt u}(2 pi) is, without any hypothesis, the Laplace transform of the GGC whose Thorin atoms are the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi). New in this book.
- [Clock of Pólya's Bessel function as a hitting time of an explicit diffusion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_of_polya_bessel_function_hitting_time_of_explicit_diffusion) (Theorem 8.7.10, page 357; proved): The index side clock of Pólya's Bessel function, the GGC with Thorin atoms at the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi), is the clock of a hitting time of a level by an explicit diffusion, planar Brownian motion killed at rate one half and Doob transformed by K_0. New in this book.
- [Sine squared forms of the Bessel clock, the drifted clock and Pólya's clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_forms_of_bessel_clock_drifted_clock_and_polya_clock) (Proposition 8.7.13, page 359; proved): The Laplace exponents of the sum of two Bessel hitting times, of the drifted first passage time and of Pólya's clock have sine squared forms whose kernels are the classical Planck and Macdonald measures and, for Pólya's clock, a completely monotone wave trace of a selfadjoint operator. New in this book.
- [Klein Gordon criterion for real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#klein_gordon_criterion_for_real_zeros) (Theorem 8.7.14, page 361; proved): If an even positive kernel is the boundary value of a solution of a Klein Gordon equation with a real potential bounded below, with the stated decay and nonvanishing conditions, then every zero of its Fourier transform is real and its square is a Dirichlet eigenvalue. New in this book.
- [De Bruijn Newman constant of Pólya's function is finite](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_bruijn_newman_constant_of_polya_function_is_finite) (Proposition 8.7.15, page 363; proved): The Gaussian deformations of Pólya's Bessel function have only real zeros exactly from a finite time Lambda_P at most zero onward, by an argument of Newman, so its de Bruijn Newman constant is not minus infinity, contrary to a conjecture of the first author's earlier note. New in this book.
- [A property that survives Gaussian damping cannot imply real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_damping_property_cannot_imply_real_zeros) (Proposition 8.7.17, page 368; proved): No property of even positive kernels that implies real zeros and survives a fixed Gaussian damping can hold for Riemann's kernel Phi, for Pólya's asymptote or for the Bessel kernel, which excludes a family of constructions with room to spare, using the theorems of Rodgers and Tao and of Newman. New in this book.
- [Open question on a diffusion for the clock of the Riemann xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_diffusion_for_clock_of_riemann_xi_function) (Question 8.7.18, page 370; open): Is there, without assuming RH, a diffusion on a half line with an entrance boundary whose hitting time of a level has the Laplace transform of the clock of Riemann's xi function scaled by four? New in this book.
- [Open question on a Klein Gordon extension of Pólya's kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_klein_gordon_extension_of_polya_kernel) (Question 8.7.19, page 370; open): Does the kernel of Riemann's xi function, rescaled, admit a Klein Gordon extension with a real potential asymptotic to e^{2x}, which would imply RH? New in this book.
- [Open question on the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_de_bruijn_newman_constants_of_polya_functions) (Question 8.7.20, page 370; open): What are the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's Bessel function and of his function Xi star, at what height do the first nonreal zeros appear, and do they appear through collisions of real zeros? New in this book.
- [Open question on a family joining the two clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_family_joining_the_two_clocks) (Question 8.7.21, page 370; open): Is there a one parameter family of laws joining the drifted first passage time and the sum of two Bessel hitting times, each member with a reciprocal symmetry encoding a functional equation, along which the index side Thorin measure can be followed? New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, Riemann xi function, clock variable, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Pólya density, Polya density, hitting time, first passage time, Keiper Li coefficients, Li criterion, de Bruijn Newman constant, Lehmer pair, Laguerre inequality, Hankel matrix, free convolution, semicircle law, Dedekind eta function, nonnegative deconvolution, backward heat flow, collision of zeros, inverse first passage problem, maximum of independent exponential variables, Bondesson class.

chapters.title: The basepoint one
chapters.summary:
This chapter works out the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint $\alpha=1$, the random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ for the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$. It asks what the Thorin measure and the law of $T_1$ are, whether the Thorin density comes from the sine squared lemma, and whether $T_1$ is a hitting time to which Kent's theorem applies. The Thorin measure of this generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is the Poisson smoothing of the zeros by Cauchy kernels, positive with no hypothesis because no zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ (the threshold theorem of Polson 2026 at $\alpha=1$). The chapter derives a Lévy form of $\log\xi(1+s)$, proves with no hypothesis (using ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts) that the Thorin density is smallest at the origin, giving an independent positive stable one half summand, and shows that this minimum at every height on every line with real part between one half and one is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). It certifies the heat trace from the primes and represents every shifted clock $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ as a subordinated hitting time of sticky Brownian motion.

#### From the literature

- $2\xi(s)$ as the Mellin transform of a sum of two Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Kent's theorem on diffusion hitting times, with Krein's inverse spectral theory (Kent 1980; Dym and McKean 1976)
- the complete Riemann zeta distribution (Nakamura 2015); Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999)
- sticky Brownian motion (Itô and McKean 1965); inverse first passage (Anulova 1980; Ekström and Janson 2016)
- verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and of GRH for the characters modulo 4 and 12 (Platt 2016); explicit zero counts (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022; Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant and Rechnitzer 2021) and bounds for $\psi(y)-y$ (Büthe 2018; Broadbent, Kadiri, Lumley, Ng and Wilk 2021; Johnston and Yang 2023)

#### New results

- [Compensated sine squared formula at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_sine_squared_formula_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.2, page 380; proved): At the basepoint one the Thorin density equals an explicit digamma expression plus a compensated sine squared sum over the primes, and the limit exists by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the completed zeta function at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_xi_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.3, page 382; proved): The logarithm of $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$ has an explicit Lévy form whose drift is the sum of the reciprocals of the zeros and whose signed Lévy measure consists of a gamma density, a pole term and prime atoms, the compensated integral converging by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and stable summand at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.4, page 385; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, certified with the first 1800 zeros in ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is smallest only at the origin, so the clock is the sum of an independent positive stable one half variable and a generalized gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [Minimum at the origin and stable summand at every basepoint from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_every_basepoint_from_one) (Proposition 9.1.5, page 388; proved): The same minimum at the origin and the same splitting into a positive stable one half summand and a generalized gamma convolution hold at every basepoint at or above one, certified with ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000. New in this book.
