- [Lévy form below the basepoint one and zero free half planes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_below_basepoint_one_and_zero_free_half_plane) (Proposition 9.1.6, page 390; proved): Below the basepoint one the Lévy form of $\xi$ converges and gives a positive Thorin density when all zeros lie to the left of the basepoint, and conversely its validity at a basepoint forces a zero free half plane to the right of it. New in this book.
- [Comparison of the Thorin density across vertical lines](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_ratio_comparison_across_vertical_lines) (Theorem 9.1.8, page 395; proved): The ratio of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed function on a vertical line to the distance of that line from the critical line is nonincreasing as the line moves right, under a hypothesis on the zeros to the right of the critical line that holds under RH, for lines at distance at least $1/\sqrt2$ from the critical line, and below the verified height. New in this book.
- [Explicit lower bound of the Thorin density by comparison with the Euler product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_lower_bound_of_thorin_density_by_comparison_with_euler_product) (Corollary 9.1.9, page 396; proved): On a line to the right of one the Euler product and the digamma function give an explicit lower bound for the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed zeta or Dirichlet L function, and under the comparison hypothesis the bound, multiplied by the ratio of the distances of the lines from the critical line, holds on every line to the left and is of order a positive multiple of the logarithm of the height. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and its equivalence with RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_below_one_equivalent_to_rh) (Theorem 9.1.11, page 397; proved): RH, respectively GRH for the Dirichlet L function of the character modulo 4 or modulo 12, is equivalent to the Thorin density of the corresponding completed function on every line with real part between one half and one being smallest at the origin and only there, a property certified in ball arithmetic with no hypothesis up to the verified height. New in this book.
- [Certified positivity of the heat trace at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_at_basepoint_one_positive_certified_from_primes) (Proposition 9.1.17, page 404; proved): The heat trace of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is certified positive at every time, with an explicit lower bound, from the primes up to ten million and published explicit bounds for Chebyshev's error, in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [No Brownian first passage to a random level at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_brownian_first_passage_to_random_level_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.2.1, page 407; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is not the first passage time of a Brownian motion with drift to a random level independent of the motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the tilted centre clock at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_subordination_of_tilted_centre_clock) (Theorem 9.2.2, page 408; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is the exponentially tilted centre clock run through the inverse local time of a sticky Brownian motion, equivalently the tilted clock plus a Brownian first passage time to a level proportional to it. New in this book.
- [Kent string hitting time of the shifted clock at the basepoint one under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_kent_string_hitting_time_under_rh) (Corollary 9.2.3, page 409; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis (every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half) and the simplicity of every nontrivial zero): Assuming RH and simple zeros, the tilted centre clock is a Kent hitting time of a Krein string with spectrum the squared moduli of the zeros, and the shifted clock at the basepoint one is the first hitting time of a level by this string diffusion run on the local time of a sticky Brownian motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the centre clock at every basepoint above the centre](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_subordination_every_basepoint_above_centre) (Theorem 9.2.5, page 415; proved): For every basepoint above the centre the shifted clock exists with no hypothesis on the zeros and is a Brownian hitting time built from the tilted centre clock, with a stable one half tail, and, by the threshold theorem of Polson 2026, it is a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. New in this book.
- [Lévy measure and self decomposability of the shifted clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_levy_measure_and_self_decomposability) (Corollary 9.2.6, page 416; proved): The shifted clock at every basepoint above the centre is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, with an explicit Lévy measure obtained from that of the centre clock. New in this book.

#### Key terms

basepoint one, shifted clock, reciprocal Xi function, completed zeta function, Thorin measure, Thorin density, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Lévy form, Levy form, sine squared lemma, Cauchy kernel, positive stable law, subordination, sticky Brownian motion, Kent's theorem, hitting time, first passage time, Wald's identity, heat trace, zero free half plane, Riemann Hypothesis, GRH

chapters.title: The critical strip and Riesz's criterion
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how much of the unconditional structure of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint one survives inside the critical strip of the Riemann zeta function, and what it says about Riesz's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Its objects are the basepoint clocks $T_\alpha$, with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, and their Thorin measures. On the real axis the reciprocal of $\xi$ is the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible normal scale mixture, an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. RH is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace of the zeros, and zero free half planes become completeness of translates of the Pólya kernel. Riesz's criterion becomes the statement that every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), and $1/\zeta(2k)$ is a Laplace transform value of the clocks. The squarefree integers, with Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$, give criteria for RH from exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed counts, a Mertens function representation and a threshold at Gamma shape two. The chapter proves no new zero free region.

#### From the literature

- Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977, 1978; Bondesson 1992).
- Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932; Kac 1965; Korevaar 1965); Salem's equivalent of RH (Salem 1953).
- Riesz's criterion (Riesz 1916) and its companion (Hardy and Littlewood 1916); Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999); the Nyman Beurling criterion (Nyman 1950; Beurling 1955; Báez Duarte 2003).
- Euler's formulae for $\zeta(2n)$ from Cauchy variables (Bourgade, Fujita and Yor 2007).
- RH verified to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).
- Squarefree integers: Math StackExchange question 2063166 (2016), the conditional exponent 7/22 (Baker and Pintz 1985), Lazarević's inequality (Lazarević 1966), integer and fractional parts (Steutel and Thiemann 1989), Ingham's method (1942); a mean square criterion the chapter calls presumably folklore.

#### New results

New in the book; the squarefree material and the Poisson trace conditions are from unpublished notes of Nicholas Polson.

- [Reciprocal Xi function on the real axis as a normal scale mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_real_axis_normal_scale_mixture) (Proposition 10.1.1, page 423; proved): For every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric, unimodal, infinitely divisible law with no hypothesis on the zeros, which has a Cauchy tail when $\alpha>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the reciprocal Xi function and the EGGC criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_thorin_form_and_eggc_criterion) (Theorem 10.1.2, page 425; proved): When every zero of $\zeta$ has real part less than the basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ (always for $\alpha\ge1$), the characteristic function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ has an explicit Thorin form with the positive density $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)/\pi$, and for $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when there is no zero to the right of $\alpha$. New in this book.
- [EGGC property of the reciprocal Xi law across the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eggc_property_across_the_critical_strip) (Theorem 10.1.3, page 428; proved): For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law $Y_\alpha$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$, and with no hypothesis its characteristic function is that of an extended generalised gamma convolution times a remainder $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)$ with $|\log\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)|\le4(|u|+u^2)\log T_0/T_0$, where $T_0\ge2$ is a height up to which all zeros lie on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_completely_monotone_iff_rh) (Corollary 10.1.4, page 431; proved): RH holds exactly when the Poisson trace $\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ of the zeros is completely monotone (the same equivalence for the heat trace was shown earlier by Polson 2026), and for $\alpha\ge1$ the corresponding trace is completely monotone with no hypothesis and decays like $b_\alpha/(\pi y)$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional range of the complete monotonicity conditions of the Poisson trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_derivative_conditions_hold_below_verified_height) (Theorem 10.1.6, page 433; proved): If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the derivative conditions $(-1)^nK^{(n)}(y)>0$ of the Poisson trace $K$ hold at every $0<y<\pi$ and every order $n<H(\pi-y)$; with $H=3\times10^{12}$ this covers all orders below $4.24\times10^{11}$ for $y\le3$. New in this book.
- [Positive definite and bounded forms of the Poisson trace criterion for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_positive_definite_and_bounded_forms_of_rh) (Proposition 10.1.7, page 435; proved): RH is equivalent to positive definiteness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ for every $x>0$, and to boundedness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ on $[0,\infty)$ for some $x>0$, where $K_{1/2}$ is the Poisson trace of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Small y asymptotics of the Poisson trace and Pólya's trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_versus_polya_trace_small_y_asymptotics) (Proposition 10.1.8, page 437; proved): As $y\to0+$ the Poisson trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ and the trace of the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ have the same main term and their difference tends to $\frac98$, with a refined second term under RH. New in this book.
- [Explicit obstruction and approximation cost for translates of the tilted Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_kernel_translates_obstruction_and_approximation_cost) (Proposition 10.1.9, page 440; proved): For translates of the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ the book proves an explicit obstruction at the centre (no finite combination approximates $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ with $L^1$ error below $\sup_\gamma|\hat g(\gamma)|$, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros on the critical line) and, where the translates are dense, an explicit cost of approximation (a combination within $\delta$ of $g$ has coefficient sum at least $(|\hat g(\gamma)|-\delta)/|\xi(\alpha+i\gamma)|$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$); the density criteria (dense exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; dense for every $\alpha>\frac12$ exactly when RH holds) restate Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932). New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel analogue of Salem's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_analogue_of_salem_criterion) (Corollary 10.1.10, page 442; proved): RH holds if and only if, for every $\frac12<\alpha<1$, the convolution equation with the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ has no bounded nonzero solution; at the centre $\cos(\gamma y)$ solves it for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Twisted Riesz function and the basepoint form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#twisted_riesz_function_and_basepoint_riesz_criterion) (Proposition 10.2.1, page 447; proved): Twisting Riesz's function by $(x/n^2)^{ih}$ changes the Gamma factor of its Mellin transform to $\Gamma(1-s+ih)/\zeta(2s)$ and keeps the criterion: $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$ exactly when $R_h(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$. New in this book.
- [The Riesz function as an average over the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_function_as_centre_clock_average) (Proposition 10.2.4, page 450; proved): With no hypothesis, Riesz's function is minus the expectation of an alternating series in the centre clock whose terms decay like $e^{-4k^2T}$ instead of $1/(k-1)!$. New in this book.
- [Riesz coefficients as values of GGC Laplace transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_coefficients_as_ggc_laplace_values) (Proposition 10.2.5, page 452; proved): For $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$, $1/\zeta(2k)$ is an explicit multiple of the Laplace transform of the basepoint clock $T_\alpha$ at $(2k-\alpha)^2$, in particular of the centre clock at $\alpha=\frac12$ and of the basepoint one clock at $\alpha=1$, and at $\alpha=1$ it is $\kappa_k$ times the exponential of minus a Thorin integral, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [GGC form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_criterion_as_ggc_property_of_basepoint_clocks) (Theorem 10.2.7, page 454; proved): Riesz's growth condition at exponent $\alpha/2$ is equivalent to each clock $T_{\alpha'}$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ being a generalised gamma convolution, to positivity of $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)$ on the lines to the right of $\alpha$, and to convergence of a compensated sine squared sum over the primes; for $\alpha=\frac12$, RH holds exactly when every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a GGC. New in this book.
- [Closed form constant of the squarefree reciprocal sum over number fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_reciprocal_sum_closed_form_constant) (Proposition 10.3.1, page 464; proved): Over a number field $K$ of degree $n\ge2$ the sum of $\mu(\mathfrak a)^2/N(\mathfrak a)$ over the integral ideals of norm at most $x$ equals $\frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}(\log x+C_K)+O(x^{-1/n}\log x)$ with the explicit constant $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$, $\gamma_K$ the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree Dirichlet series as a gamma factor times a ratio of Pólya moment generating functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_dirichlet_series_as_gamma_factor_times_polya_ratio) (Proposition 10.3.3, page 466; proved): The squarefree Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$ equals an explicit gamma factor times $\mathbb{E}\,e^{(s-1/2)X}/\mathbb{E}\,e^{(2s-1/2)X}$ for the Pólya variable $X$, which continues the series to every $s$ with $\xi(2s)\ne0$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant as a combination of two tilted Pólya means](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_as_difference_of_tilted_polya_means) (Theorem 10.3.5, page 467; proved): The constant $C$ of the squarefree reciprocal sum is an elementary part plus $b_1-2b_2$, a combination of the means of the Pólya variable tilted at the basepoints one and two, which is an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Dedekind zeta clock is a GGC if and only if RH holds for the field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dedekind_clock_is_ggc_iff_rh_for_dedekind_zeta) (Proposition 10.3.6, page 469; proved): For a number field $K$ with $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$, the reciprocal of the normalised completed Dedekind function is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_K$ lie on the critical line, with Thorin measure the sum of point masses at the squared ordinates; this is the number field form of the rigidity theorem of Polson 2026. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant of a number field through the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_of_a_number_field_through_zeros) (Theorem 10.3.7, page 470; proved): For a number field $K$ the constant $C_K$ is an explicit elementary term $A_K$ plus an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function, and under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$ that sum is a combination of two Stieltjes transform values of the Thorin measure. New in this book.
- [Exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree counts are equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#smoothed_squarefree_counts_equivalent_to_rh) (Theorem 10.3.9, page 473; proved): RH holds if and only if the squarefree count smoothed by an exponential law, or by a Gamma(2) law, with mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and under RH with simple zeros an explicit formula with exponentially damped terms at the zeros holds. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the squarefree error of the order of the fourth root of x](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_lower_bound_order_fourth_root_of_x) (Corollary 10.3.11, page 476; proved): With no hypothesis the squarefree error $\Delta(x)$ satisfies $\limsup\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge0.1004$ and $\liminf\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-0.1004$, so the order $x^{1/4}$ cannot be lowered, and the Gamma(2) smoothed error has the same property with constant $9.94\times10^{-5}$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree count at a Gamma(n) random point under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_gamma_n_smoothing_bound_under_rh) (Proposition 10.3.12, page 477; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis): Under RH, the expected squarefree count at a Gamma($n$) random point of mean $x$ is $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}n^{1/8+\varepsilon})$, uniformly in $n\ge1$. New in this book.
- [Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as a positive average of the Mertens function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma2_smoothed_squarefree_error_as_mertens_average) (Theorem 10.3.15, page 479; proved): The squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2$ minus half the expected Mertens function at the random point $\sqrt{x\mathcal{V}_2/2}$, where the density $f_2$ of $\mathcal{V}_2$ is explicit and positive by Lazarević's inequality. New in this book.
- [Gamma smoothing threshold, shape two](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_smoothing_threshold_shape_two) (Theorem 10.3.18, page 482; proved): The signed density that mixes the Mertens function in the Gamma($\nu$) smoothed squarefree error is nonnegative exactly for the shapes $\nu\in(0,2]$, the obstruction above two being the trivial zero of $\zeta$ at $-2$. New in this book.
- [Pointwise bound for the squarefree error under RH (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_pointwise_bound_under_rh_open) (Question 10.3.19, page 484; open): The book asks for a proof, under RH, that the squarefree count has error $O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$, and records forms equivalent to it or sufficient for it. New in this book.
- [Sharpening the lower bound constant for the squarefree error (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_fejer_constant_and_unboundedness_open) (Question 10.3.20, page 485; open): The book asks whether a Fejér kernel over many zeros improves the constant $0.1004$ in the lower bound for the squarefree error, and whether $\limsup|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}$ is infinite. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riesz criterion, Riemann hypothesis, critical strip, reciprocal Xi function, basepoint clock, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, extended generalised gamma convolution, EGGC, normal scale mixture, Poisson trace, complete monotonicity, Wiener closure theorem, Salem criterion, Pólya kernel, Möbius function, squarefree integers, square free numbers, Mertens function, Gamma smoothing, Dedekind zeta function, Nyman Beurling criterion

chapters.title: Infinite divisibility, the eta analogue and almost generalised gamma convolutions
chapters.summary:
What can be said about the Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function without a zero free half plane? The centre clock is self decomposable and unimodal with no hypothesis, and the tilted Pólya variable is quasi infinitely divisible above the basepoint one and not at it. The Upsilon transform and the Bercovici Pata bijection give the clock a free counterpart, and RH holds exactly when the clock is the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law. A Wiener gamma integral and a Riemann Ornstein Uhlenbeck process realise the laws as processes. A Dedekind eta analogue treats the Dirichlet L function of the real character modulo 12, whose completed function has no pole. The almost GGC theorem uses zero density estimates to show, with no hypothesis, that every shifted clock is a generalized gamma convolution up to a defect carried by the zeros to its right, whose Cauchy kernels carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the others, with a power saving; the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ bounds the defect explicitly. The last section treats Pakes's Lambert law, Urbanik's classes ($L_2$ but not $L_3$) and a criticality filter.

#### From the literature

Self decomposable laws and GGCs (Sato 1999; Bondesson 1992), driving subordinators (Wolfe 1982; Jurek and Vervaat 1983), unimodality (Yamazato 1978), subexponential tails (Embrechts, Goldie and Veraverbeke 1979); quasi infinite divisibility (Lindner, Pan and Sato 2018), proved above the basepoint one by Nakamura (2015); Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Bercovici Pata bijection (Bercovici and Pata 1999), free regular laws (Arizmendi, Hasebe and Sakuma 2013), free self decomposability (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2002), its unimodality (Hasebe and Thorbjørnsen 2016), Upsilon transform (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2004; Barndorff-Nielsen, Maejima and Sato 2006), finite free convolution (Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2022); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; Guth and Maynard 2026); verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Steutel's conjecture on Gamma(2) scale mixtures (Kristiansen 1994); size biasing theorem (Steutel 1973); nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020); the Lambert law as a GGC (Pakes 2011; Kalugin, Jeffrey and Corless 2012) and ladders of self decomposable laws (Pakes 2026); Urbanik's classes (Urbanik 1973).

#### New results

- [Background driving subordinator of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_background_driving_subordinator) (Proposition 11.1.1, page 489; proved): With no hypothesis the centre clock is the integral of $e^{-t}$ against a subordinator whose Lévy density is minus the derivative of the heat trace of the zeros, and RH holds if and only if that density is completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Unimodality of the centre clock and the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_and_shifted_clocks_unimodal) (Corollary 11.1.2, page 491; proved): The centre clock and every shifted clock with basepoint above one half have unimodal laws, with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one is not quasi infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_tilt_basepoint_one_not_quasi_infinitely_divisible) (Proposition 11.1.3, page 495; proved): The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one, with moment generating function $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$, is not quasi infinitely divisible, hence not infinitely divisible. New in this book.
- [Thorin Bernstein form of the shifted clock criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_bernstein_criterion_for_shifted_clock_exponent) (Proposition 11.1.4, page 498; proved): The Laplace exponent of the shifted clock is a Thorin Bernstein function with no hypothesis when the basepoint is at least one, and for basepoints between one half and one exactly when zeta has no zero to the right of the basepoint, while the exponent of the centre clock is one if and only if RH holds. New in this book.
- [Upsilon image and free counterpart of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#upsilon_image_and_free_counterpart_of_centre_clock) (Theorem 11.2.3, page 513; proved): With no hypothesis the Upsilon image of the centre clock is a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin measure and its Bercovici Pata counterpart is a freely self decomposable unimodal law carried by a half line $[c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, and RH holds if and only if the clock is itself the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law. New in this book.
- [Peeling a gamma layer from the Pólya generating function keeps zeros real under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_layer_peeling_keeps_real_zeros_under_rh) (Proposition 11.2.8, page 525; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis): If RH holds, dividing the Taylor coefficients of the Pólya generating function by $(a)_k$ keeps all zeros real and negative for every $a>0$, whereas multiplying the coefficients of a polynomial by $(a)_k$ need not preserve real zeros. New in this book.
- [No gamma scale mixture for the Pólya variable and Williams' variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gamma_scale_mixture_for_polya_and_williams_variables) (Theorem 11.2.9, page 526; proved): For no shape $a>0$ is the absolute value of the Pólya variable, its square or Williams' variable $S_2$ a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eta_analogue_thorin_measure_positive_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 11.3.1, page 531; proved): For the L function of the real character modulo 12, the reciprocal completed function at the basepoint one is the Laplace transform of a GGC with an explicit positive Thorin density, with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eta_analogue_levy_form_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 11.3.2, page 532; proved): For the completed L function of the real character modulo 12, the logarithm of $\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})/\xi(1,\chi_{12})$ has an explicit Lévy form, with a positive gamma density and prime atoms of both signs, that needs no compensation by a pole term. New in this book.
- [Almost GGC theorem for the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#almost_ggc_theorem) (Theorem 11.4.2, page 541; proved): With no hypothesis, for every basepoint between one half and one the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of the basepoint carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the kernels of the other zeros, with a power saving from zero density estimates. New in this book.
- [Canonical factorisation of the shifted clock transform into a GGC and a defect](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#canonical_factorisation_of_shifted_clock_transform) (Proposition 11.4.3, page 542; proved): The Laplace transform of the shifted clock factorises exactly as the transform of a GGC times an explicit defect that carries every zero to the right of the basepoint and equals one if and only if there is none. New in this book.
- [Explicit bounds on the defect from the verification of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_defect_bounds_from_rh_verification) (Theorem 11.4.4, page 543; proved): Using the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, with part of the proof certified in ball arithmetic, the defect of the shifted clock is within $e^{\pm1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}$ of one and the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $1.5\times10^{12}$ once the basepoint exceeds one half by more than $6\times10^{-10}$. New in this book.
- [Positivity of the Thorin density on the verified window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_positive_on_verified_window) (Corollary 11.4.5, page 545; proved): For every basepoint above one half the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $3\times10^{12}$ minus one half, and for basepoints up to $7.35$ it is smallest at the origin up to the height $3\times10^{12}-(1+\sqrt{2})/2$. New in this book.
- [Size biased clock and the exponential mixture form of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#size_biased_clock_decomposition_exponential_mixture_iff_rh) (Proposition 11.5.1, page 560; proved): With no hypothesis the size biased clock is the clock plus an independent variable whose density is the heat trace divided by its integral, and RH holds exactly when that variable is a mixture of exponential laws (Steutel's decomposition applied to the clock). New in this book.
- [Centre clock lies in Urbanik class L2 and not in L3](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_urbanik_class_l2_not_l3) (Theorem 11.5.8, page 569; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, and certified in ball arithmetic, the centre clock lies in Urbanik's class $L_2$ and not in $L_3$, because the third ladder function of the heat trace is positive while the fourth is negative at $e^{-4.15}$. New in this book.
- [First two driving processes of the clock are self decomposable and unimodal](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_first_two_driving_processes_self_decomposable_unimodal) (Corollary 11.5.10, page 572; proved): With no hypothesis, at every time the laws of the driving process of the clock and of the driving process of that process are self decomposable, hence unimodal, and the first lies in Urbanik's class $L_1$. New in this book.
- [The clock is not the martingale limit of a supercritical continuous state branching process](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_not_supercritical_csbp_martingale_limit) (Theorem 11.5.13, page 577; proved): Certified in ball arithmetic, the sixteenth Taylor coefficient of the function $g$ built from the clock has the wrong sign, so no positive multiple of the clock is the martingale limit of a supercritical continuous state branching process with finite Malthusian parameter. New in this book.
- [Criticality filter for properties of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#criticality_filter_damped_polya_kernel) (Proposition 11.5.14, page 579; proved): By the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative, no property shared by the damped Pólya kernels with $t<0$ (such as positivity, monotonicity, log concavity, double exponential decay or analyticity in a strip) can imply real zeros of the transform or that the normalised reciprocal of the transform on the imaginary axis is the Laplace transform of a GGC. New in this book.
- [Damped Pólya law as a mixture of arcsine laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_polya_law_arcsine_mixture) (Proposition 11.5.15, page 581; proved): For every $t\le0$ the Pólya law damped by $e^{tv^2/4}$ is a mixture of arcsine laws with an explicit positive mixing density, extending to all $t\le0$ the arcsine representation of the Pólya variable at $t=0$ (the arcsine route of Polson 2026). New in this book.
- [Tilted Biane Pitman Yor variable is not a GGC near t = 0 and at ten certified values of t](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#biane_pitman_yor_lognormal_tilt_not_ggc_near_zero) (Proposition 11.5.17, page 583; proved): It is certified that the Biane Pitman Yor variable, which is a GGC, stops being a GGC after the lognormal tilt $e^{t(\log b)^2/16}$ for ten listed values of $t$ and for every sufficiently small $t\ne0$. New in this book.
- [Theta variable of the odd real character modulo 8 and its reciprocal are not GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_variable_character_minus_8_not_ggc) (Proposition 11.5.20, page 587; counterexample, proved): It is certified that neither the theta variable of the real odd character of discriminant $-8$ nor its reciprocal is a GGC, so the theta variable of an $L$ function with an Euler product need not have the GGC property. New in this book.
- [Reciprocal theta variable of odd characters is a GGC for discriminants -3 and -4, not for -8, for d congruent to 1 mod 8 and for the function of Davenport and Heilbronn](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_odd_character_reciprocal_laplace_transform) (Proposition 11.5.21, page 588; proved): For an odd theta type coefficient sequence the Laplace transform of the reciprocal theta variable is a ratio of hyperbolic sines (after Biane, Pitman and Yor), which gives the GGC property for the characters of discriminant $-3$ and $-4$ and its failure for discriminant $-8$, for odd characters of discriminant $d\equiv1 \pmod 8$ and for the function of Davenport and Heilbronn. New in this book.
- [Open problem on theta type functions whose GGC property forces zeros onto the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ggc_class_theta_functions_zeros_on_line) (Problem 11.1, page 591; open): It is an open problem to find a natural class of theta type functions containing the Riemann xi function in which a GGC theta variable forces all zeros onto the critical line (which would prove RH), or a function in such a class with a GGC theta variable and a zero off the line. New in this book.
- [Open problem, is the tilted Biane Pitman Yor variable a GGC for no t other than 0](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_biane_pitman_yor_tilt_ggc_for_no_t) (Problem 11.2, page 592; open): It is an open problem whether the Biane Pitman Yor variable tilted by $e^{t(\log b)^2/16}$ fails to be a GGC for every $t\ne0$, which is known only for small $|t|$ and for ten listed values of $t$. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the GGC property of theta variables of characters](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ggc_theta_variables_of_passing_characters) (Problem 11.3, page 592; open): It is an open problem which of the theta variables of the real characters of discriminant $-4$, $-3$, $5$, $8$ and $12$, all of which pass the numerical GGC test to order 12, are GGCs. New in this book.
- [Open problem on unconditional positivity of the Li coefficients](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_li_coefficients_unconditional_positivity_size_biased_clock) (Problem 11.4, page 592; open): It is an open problem which unconditional properties of the heat trace or of the size biased clock variable force the Li coefficients to be nonnegative for every $n$, which would prove RH by Li's criterion. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the ladder index along the de Bruijn Newman flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ladder_index_along_de_bruijn_newman_flow) (Problem 11.5, page 592; open): It is an open problem to describe the ladder index of the laws with Laplace transform $R_t$ along the de Bruijn Newman flow, which numerically drops from two to one between $t=27.8$ and $t=27.9$, and to decide whether it is nonincreasing in $t$ and equal to one for all large $t$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, Thorin measure, shifted clock, self decomposable, quasi infinitely divisible, Upsilon transform, Bercovici Pata bijection, free probability, semicircle law, finite free convolution, Dedekind eta function, Lambert W function, Urbanik class, Riemann Hypothesis

chapters.title: Conclusions and open problems
chapters.summary:
How far does the Thorin approach to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) reach, and what can computation add? The chapter summarises the book and sets out a path along the basepoint α of the shifted clock of the reciprocal Xi function, with Laplace transform ξ(α)/ξ(α+√u). For α ≥ 1 it is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with positive Thorin measure, with no hypothesis. For 1/2 < α < 1 the GGC property is equivalent to a zero free half plane Re s > α, and at the centre it is RH (Lagarias positivity). The gap is one positivity statement uniform in the height and the resolution. The chapter discusses the zero free half plane Re s > 7/8 announced in October 2026, the sine squared lemma, five computational work packages (among them certified Thorin densities in ball arithmetic, twisted Riesz filters, margins against the circular unitary ensemble, the almost GGC defect), closed routes, the reach of finite information (a perturbation theorem with off line zeros) and what a proof must supply. It poses six open problems from free probability, on Jensen polynomials, Laguerre expansions, Jacobi parameters, the Hankel test and zero collisions along the de Bruijn Newman flow, and the heat trace ladder.

#### From the literature

The Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992). The criteria of Riesz (1916), Weil (1952), Li (1997; Keiper 1992) and Lagarias (1999). The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Rodgers and Tao 2020; Platt and Trudgian 2021). Conrey and Li (2000) on a false positivity condition. Zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; Guth and Maynard 2026). RH verified to height 3 × 10^12 (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Odlyzko's tables of zeros (1987; 2001). The finite free convolution (Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2022) and the Upsilon transform (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2004). The half plane Re s > 7/8 is announced by OpenAI (2026), not refereed.

#### New results

This chapter summarises results proved earlier; its catalogued entries are open problems.

- [Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moments as finite free products (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_jensen_polynomials_as_finite_free_products) (Problem 12.1, page 609; open): Find factorisations of the normalised coefficients of the Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moment sequence into two real rooted polynomials, which would give real zeros, or show that none exist with factors of a given kind. New in this book.
- [Laguerre and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of the Pólya density (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_laguerre_meixner_pollaczek_expansions_of_polya_density) (Problem 12.2, page 609; open): Find a variable in which the Pólya density or the Xi function has an expansion in Laguerre or Meixner Pollaczek polynomials with positive coefficients and truncations with only real zeros. New in this book.
- [Jacobi parameters of the zero measure and the local semicircle model (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_jacobi_parameters_of_zero_measure_and_local_semicircle_model) (Problem 12.3, page 609; open): Prove under the Riemann Hypothesis that the Jacobi parameters of the measure of the inverse squared ordinates satisfy alpha_n ~ 2 beta_n ~ L_n/2, a spectral form of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula, and explain the scatter of the ratios. New in this book.
- [Order at which a zero collision is registered by the Hankel test (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_order_at_which_a_zero_collision_is_registered_by_hankel_test) (Problem 12.4, page 609; open): Find the rule giving the order of the Hankel matrix at which the collision of a pair of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow is registered, and follow the failure times of the Hankel test to orders of a few hundred. New in this book.
- [Unconditional brackets for the collision times of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_unconditional_collision_brackets_for_de_bruijn_newman_flow) (Problem 12.5, page 610; open): Find a priori control of the nonreal zeros of the heat evolved Xi function at negative times so that the book's brackets for collision times become statements computed from the Xi function at time zero alone. New in this book.
- [Extending the derivative sign ladder of the heat trace without new information on the zeros (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_moving_derivative_sign_ladder_of_heat_trace_without_new_zeros) (Problem 12.6, page 610; open): Find a mechanism, for instance a functional equation for the law of the clock under the Upsilon transform, that extends the proved ranges of derivative signs of the heat trace without further information on the zeros. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, shifted clock, reciprocal Xi function, basepoint, sine squared lemma, zero free half plane, de Bruijn Newman constant, Riesz criterion, Lagarias positivity, Jensen polynomials, ball arithmetic

chapters.title: Ferromagnetic random variables
chapters.summary:
Which random variables are ferromagnetic, and is the Pólya law ferromagnetic? A symmetric random variable is ferromagnetic if its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis, the Lee and Yang property of a single Ising spin. The Pólya variable has density p = Φ/Ξ(0) and moment generating function ξ(1/2+s)/ξ(1/2), so the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) says exactly that it is ferromagnetic. The chapter develops the class: the clock (a generalised gamma convolution, GGC, with one Thorin atom per pair of zeros, giving a van Dantzig pair), closure under weak limits (RH holds if and only if the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws), mixtures of uniform laws (the shoulder theorem) and the absence of a Gaussian component. It builds ferromagnetic approximations of the Pólya law within total variation distance 2 × 10^-6, certified in ball arithmetic, and shows that RH is equivalent to an identity in law with a series of Maxwell variables. It studies e^{2X}, a size biased variable of Biane, Pitman and Yor: not a GGC, self decomposable, with hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) powers e^{βX} for |β| ≥ 5.5791422, by a computer assisted proof in ball arithmetic.

#### From the literature

The Lee and Yang theorem (Lee and Yang 1952); Newman's single spin laws, Hadamard form and cumulants (Newman 1974; 1975); Lieb and Sokal (1981). The Griffiths Simon and Ellis, Monroe and Newman classes (Simon and Griffiths 1973; Ellis, Monroe and Newman 1976) and the GHS inequality for the Pólya law (Newman 1991). Van Dantzig pairs (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024). Pólya's theorems on real zeros (1918; 1926); de Bruijn's strip theorem (1950); Turán inequalities (Csordas, Norfolk and Varga 1986); Jensen polynomials (Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier 2019). The Biane, Pitman and Yor variable (2001), Kent (1978), Fourati (2016). The half plane Re s > 7/8 is announced by OpenAI (2026), not refereed.

#### New results

The results of this chapter are proved (one is a counterexample and one is conditional on the announced zero free half plane Re s > 7/8) or are open problems.

- [Clock and van Dantzig partner of a ferromagnetic law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_law_clock_and_van_dantzig_partner) (Theorem 13.1.4, page 618; proved): The clock of a ferromagnetic law is a generalised gamma convolution with drift equal to the Gaussian part and one unit Thorin atom at the square of each positive zero of its characteristic function, and the law has a partner of Pólya frequency type forming a van Dantzig pair with it. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic laws are closed under convergence in law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_laws_closed_under_convergence_in_law) (Theorem 13.1.5, page 620; proved): A limit in law of ferromagnetic random variables is ferromagnetic, the variances converge and the moment generating functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane. New in this book.
- [RH holds exactly when the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_polya_law_is_a_limit_in_law_of_ferromagnetic_laws) (Corollary 13.1.7, page 621; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the Pólya law being a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws. New in this book.
- [A uniform law mixed with an atom at the origin is not ferromagnetic](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mixture_of_uniform_law_with_atom_at_origin_is_not_ferromagnetic) (Theorem 13.2.1, page 622; counterexample, proved): The mixture of the uniform law on [-1,1] and a point mass at the origin is symmetric and unimodal but not ferromagnetic, so mixtures of ferromagnetic laws need not be ferromagnetic. New in this book.
- [Shoulder theorem for symmetric laws on an interval](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shoulder_theorem_for_ferromagnetic_laws_on_an_interval) (Theorem 13.2.3, page 623; proved): A symmetric density on [-1,1] that vanishes at plus and minus 1 and is nonincreasing on [0,1] gives a ferromagnetic law if it is concave on [0,1], and does not if it is convex on [0,1] and not linear on its support. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic laws among the kernels 1 minus |x|^b, k monotone kernels and products of uniform laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_laws_among_power_kernels_and_products_of_uniform_laws) (Corollary 13.2.4, page 624; proved): The law with density proportional to 1 minus |x|^b is ferromagnetic exactly when b is at least 1, the k monotone kernel exactly when k is at most 2, the densities (1 minus x squared) to the power m with 0 < m at most 1 are ferromagnetic, and a product of two independent uniform variables is not. New in this book.
- [Densities nondecreasing in |x| and mixtures of uniform laws on shells are ferromagnetic](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shell_mixtures_of_uniform_laws_are_ferromagnetic) (Theorem 13.2.5, page 625; proved): Every symmetric density on [-1,1] that is nondecreasing in |x|, equivalently every mixture of uniform laws on the shells a at most |x| at most 1, is ferromagnetic. New in this book.
- [The Pólya law has no Gaussian component and no ferromagnetic summand with finitely many zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_law_has_no_gaussian_component_and_no_finite_zero_summand) (Theorem 13.3.1, page 631; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, an independent summand of a symmetric law whose log moment generating function is o(s^2) has log moment generating function o(s^2) as well, so the Pólya law has no Gaussian component and is not a sum of independent ferromagnetic variables one of which is nonzero with finitely many zeros. New in this book.
- [Cosine and Gaussian tilts of the Pólya law with variance at least 9/64 if there is no zero beyond 7/8](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_and_gaussian_tilts_of_polya_law_ferromagnetic_if_no_zero_beyond_seven_eighths) (Proposition 13.4.2, page 633; conditional on The Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8 (announced by OpenAI in October 2026, not refereed, and not proved in the book)): If the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part above 7/8, then tilting the Pólya density by cosh(at) with a at least 3/8, or by other multipliers of variance at least 9/64, gives a ferromagnetic law, against 1/2 and 1/4 with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Zero completed laws of the Pólya variable, the Maxwell construction and a criterion for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_completed_laws_maxwell_construction_and_rh_criterion) (Theorem 13.4.3, page 635; proved): Keeping the first K zero factors of the Pólya characteristic function and a Gaussian factor gives laws that are exactly ferromagnetic for K up to 16 by a Maxwell construction with a certified inequality, ferromagnetic whenever nonnegative, and whose characteristic functions converge to that of the Pólya law exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to an identity in law between the smoothed Pólya variable and a series of Maxwell variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_polya_variable_smoothed_by_gaussian_equals_maxwell_series_in_law) (Theorem 13.4.5, page 638; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya variable plus an independent Gaussian of half its variance has the law of the series of independent Maxwell variables divided by the ordinates of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_law_within_total_variation_two_millionths_of_a_ferromagnetic_law) (Proposition 13.4.6, page 639; proved): With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds. New in this book.
- [Powers of the exponential of the Pólya variable are not infinitely divisible for exponent below 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#powers_of_exponential_of_polya_variable_not_infinitely_divisible_below_two) (Proposition 13.5.1, page 640; proved): For every real beta with 0 less than |beta| less than 2 the variable e to the beta X is not infinitely divisible, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [The exponential of the Pólya variable is not a generalised gamma convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_of_polya_variable_is_not_a_generalised_gamma_convolution) (Theorem 13.5.3, page 642; proved): Size biasing the Biane Pitman Yor variable (pi/2) S_2 by a power q in (0,1) destroys the generalised gamma convolution property, and in particular e to the 2X is not a generalised gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [Size bias principle for sums of gamma variables with integer shapes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#size_bias_principle_for_sums_of_gamma_variables_with_integer_shapes) (Theorem 13.5.5, page 643; proved): Size biasing a sum of independent gamma variables with integer shapes by a power q in (0,1) raises every shape by q at the cost of an independent generalised gamma convolution that puts mass q on each gap between consecutive rates. New in this book.
- [Factorisation of the exponential of the Pólya variable against a Biane Pitman Yor variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#factorisation_of_exponential_of_polya_variable_against_biane_pitman_yor_variable) (Theorem 13.5.6, page 645; proved): Adding an independent generalised gamma convolution without drift to the size biased Biane Pitman Yor variable B_q gives (pi/2) S_{2+q}, and in particular e to the 2X plus an independent generalised gamma convolution has the law of (pi/2) S_{9/4}. New in this book.
- [The exponential of the Pólya variable is self decomposable with a Lévy density built from the theta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_of_polya_variable_self_decomposable_with_theta_levy_density) (Theorem 13.5.7, page 646; proved): The size biased Biane Pitman Yor variable B_q is self decomposable with a Lévy density built from the theta function, between 2 omega(x)/x and (2+q) omega(x)/x, so e to the 2X is self decomposable, hence infinitely divisible and unimodal, without being a generalised gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [Hyperbolically completely monotone densities of the powers of the exponential of the Pólya variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hyperbolically_completely_monotone_powers_of_exponential_of_polya_variable) (Proposition 13.5.8, page 648; proved): The power e to the beta X of the exponential of the Pólya variable has a hyperbolically completely monotone density, so it is a generalised gamma convolution, for |beta| at least 5.5791422 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic, and has none for |beta| at most 5.5791395. New in this book.
- [Mixed shoulders and the sine transform of the slope (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_mixed_shoulders_sine_transform_of_slope) (Problem 13.1, page 650; open): Decide which symmetric densities on an interval whose slope first rises and then falls give ferromagnetic laws, beyond the symmetric slopes settled in the book; on the half line the slope of the Pólya density also rises and then falls, and the Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that its sine transform has only real zeros. New in this book.
- [Does the Pólya law belong to the Griffiths Simon class (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_polya_law_in_griffiths_simon_class) (Problem 13.2, page 650; open): Decide whether the Pólya law is a weak limit of suitably scaled sums of ferromagnetically coupled Ising spins, a positive answer to which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Splitting the zeros of the Pólya characteristic function into two characteristic functions (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_splitting_the_zeros_into_two_characteristic_functions) (Problem 13.3, page 650; open): Under the Riemann Hypothesis, decide whether the ordinates can be split into two nonempty sets, each giving a product that is a characteristic function. New in this book.
- [Positivity of the zero completed laws and the threshold near K = 5000 (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_positivity_of_zero_completed_laws_and_the_threshold_v_star) (Problem 13.4, page 650; open): Compute the positivity threshold of the zero completed laws near K equal to 5000, where two fits to the ratio of the threshold to the Gaussian variance part ways, and decide whether every zero completed law is a probability density. New in this book.
- [The cosine constant Omega, whether the good tilts form an interval, and improved bounds (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_cosine_constant_omega_interval_and_improved_bounds) (Problem 13.5, page 651; open): Decide whether the set of a for which the cosh(at) tilt of the Pólya density is ferromagnetic is an interval, and improve the bounds Omega at most 1/2, and at most 3/8 if there is no zero beyond 7/8, by computation with the zeros. New in this book.
- [The size bias principle for real shapes (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_size_bias_principle_for_real_shapes) (Problem 13.6, page 651; open): Decide whether the size bias principle for sums of gamma variables, proved for integer shapes, holds for all real shapes, which needs above all that the phase of the Laplace transform fall by exactly q on each gap. New in this book.
- [Infinite divisibility of powers of the exponential of the Pólya variable below the HCM threshold (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_powers_of_exponential_of_polya_variable_below_hcm_threshold) (Problem 13.7, page 651; open): For exponents between 2 and the HCM threshold, decide whether the power of the exponential of the Pólya variable is infinitely divisible, self decomposable or a generalised gamma convolution, and whether the HCM threshold equals pi over v_m. New in this book.

#### Key terms

ferromagnetic random variable, ferromagnetic law, Lee and Yang property, Ising model, Pólya law, Polya law, van Dantzig pair, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, self decomposable, hyperbolically completely monotone, HCM, size bias, Maxwell variable, total variation distance

chapters.title: The Pólya density as a maximum order statistic and the Thorin measure of the clock
chapters.summary:
Which parts of the maximum structure behind the Pólya density of Riemann's xi function survive the passage to the Thorin measure of the clock? The Pólya kernel comes from the density of the square root of a sum of two independent copies of the maximum $M_4$ of independent exponential variables, while the clock $1/G(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$ is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds. The chapter factors the tilted maximum through the zeta distribution of Khinchin, sets the maximum and the clock in the language of Wald couples, and proves a Stieltjes criterion for RH in which an off line zero appears as an atom of negative mass. It gives an explicit GGC within a stated Laplace distance of the clock, its Gumbel norming constant from the first zero, its finite order Bondesson and hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) properties, with RH equivalent to the infinite order versions, and a finite arithmetic form of the basepoint density below $\alpha=1$. The symmetrised finite stages of the maximum give, through Hurwitz's theorem, a sufficient condition for RH. The clock is not a maximum of independent exponential variables: the maximum structure belongs to the theta function and not to the zeros. It examines three reformulations of RH and finds that none is a new path, poses four open problems, and claims no proof of RH.

#### From the literature

- the law with moments $2\xi(s)$ as, up to a constant factor, the maximum of a normalised Brownian excursion (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- the zeta distribution and the infinite divisibility of $\zeta(\sigma+it)/\zeta(\sigma)$ for $\sigma>1$ (Khinchin 1938; Gnedenko and Kolmogorov 1954; Lin and Hu 2001)
- the logistic law as a normal scale mixture (Andrews and Mallows 1974; Stefanski 1991); van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968); Wald couples (Polson 2018)
- the limit laws of maxima (Gnedenko 1943); Bondesson's theorem that GGC Laplace transforms are the HCM functions (Bondesson 1992)
- Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020); RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ and $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- zeros of sections of $\zeta$ (Turán 1948; Montgomery 1983), also symmetrised (Spira 1967; Gonek and Montgomery 2013)

#### New results

Theorems are proved, the finite arithmetic form below $\alpha=1$ is conditional, and the problems are open.

- [Pólya kernel from a sum of two maxima of exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_from_sum_of_two_maxima_of_exponentials) (Proposition 14.2.1, page 657; proved): The square e^{2Y} of the variable e^Y built from Riemann's xi function has the law of a sum of two independent copies of the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, and the Pólya kernel is recovered from the density of the square root of that sum by an explicit change of variables. New in this book.
- [Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum of exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#khinchin_factorisation_of_tilted_maximum_of_exponentials) (Theorem 14.3.1, page 659; proved): For sigma above one, the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, tilted by the factor m^{sigma/2} and multiplied by an independent geometric factor 4^{-K} that modifies only the prime 2, has the law of a gamma variable divided by pi times the square of a zeta distributed integer. New in this book.
- [Wald couples of the maximum of exponential variables and the logistic law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#wald_couples_of_maximum_of_exponentials_and_logistic_law) (Theorem 14.4.2, page 660; proved): The maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, paired with a uniform variable on (-1,1) scaled by the square root of pi over two, is a Wald couple, as is the pair of sums of two independent copies, and the square root of M_4 times a standard normal variable has the logistic law. The van Dantzig pair involved is classical and the logistic statement is due to Andrews and Mallows and to Stefanski; the book's addition is their reading through the maximum in the language of Wald couples. New in this book.
- [Stieltjes criterion for RH through the smoothed Thorin density of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#stieltjes_criterion_for_rh_through_smoothed_thorin_density_of_clock) (Theorem 14.6.1, page 661; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to each of the following: the clock is a GGC, the function G'/G, minus the logarithmic derivative of its transform 1/G, is a Stieltjes function, its heat trace W is completely monotone, and the smoothed Thorin density r_eta(x), the imaginary part of G'/G at minus x minus i eta divided by pi, is nonnegative for all real x and all eta above zero. The form through r_eta is new, and the others are in the book. New in this book.
- [An off line zero makes the smoothed Thorin density of the clock negative](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_zero_makes_smoothed_thorin_density_of_clock_negative) (Lemma 14.6.2, page 662; proved): If a zero has real part beta above one half and ordinate gamma, the smoothed Thorin density r_eta of the clock at the point gamma squared minus delta squared, with delta equal to beta minus one half, tends to minus infinity as eta increases to twice delta times gamma. An explicit formula gives its value for eta below that and shows when it is negative. New in this book.
- [An explicit GGC within a stated Laplace distance of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_ggc_within_laplace_distance_of_the_clock) (Proposition 14.7.2, page 664; proved): The sum of independent exponential variables divided by the squares of the ordinates of the zeros up to height 3 times 10^12 is a GGC whose Laplace transform is within 2.5 times 10^-11 of the transform of the clock, by a certified bound that uses the verification of RH up to that height and nothing about the zeros above it. New in this book.
- [Term of one zero in the Thorin density of the basepoint family in the lambda chart](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#term_of_one_zero_in_thorin_density_of_basepoint_family_lambda_chart) (Proposition 14.8.1, page 666; proved): In the Laplace variable lambda the term of a single zero in the Thorin density at basepoint alpha is a sum of two Poisson kernels divided by twice the square root of lambda. It equals a factor kappa above one times a function that is a Cauchy density when delta is positive, has total mass the sign of delta, and near its peak is a Lorentzian of full width 4 |delta| gamma up to a relative error of order delta squared over gamma squared. New in this book.
- [The clock is not a maximum of independent exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_is_not_a_maximum_of_independent_exponential_variables) (Proposition 14.9.1, page 671; proved): The negative logarithm of the distribution function of the clock is not completely monotone, so the clock is not the maximum of independent exponential variables with any rates, nor of a Poisson cloud of exponential clocks. The proof compares the first two exponential terms of the tail of the clock, and the coefficient of the second is negative where complete monotonicity would force it to be nonnegative. New in this book.
- [Gumbel limit for maxima of independent copies of the clock and of the maximum M_4](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gumbel_limit_for_maxima_of_independent_copies_of_the_clock) (Proposition 14.10.1, page 672; proved): The maximum of n independent copies of the clock, scaled by the square of the first zero ordinate and centred at an explicit logarithm, converges to the Gumbel law, and divided by log n it tends to the reciprocal of that square; the maximum of n copies of M_4, scaled by pi and centred at log(2n), has the same Gumbel limit. This is Gnedenko's theorem applied to the exponential tails of M_4 and of the clock; the book's addition is the reading of the norming constant of the clock as the first atom of its Thorin measure, with the constant given by the first residue. New in this book.
- [Convergence of the finite maxima and of the finite stages of xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_maxima_converge_to_maximum_and_finite_stages_to_xi) (Theorem 14.12.1, page 676; proved): Truncating the maximum M_4 at N exponential variables of each kind gives a maximum that differs from M_4 only on an event of probability at most C sqrt(N) e^{-pi sqrt(N)/2}, and the finite stage xi_N of the xi function and its symmetrisation converge to xi uniformly on compact subsets of the open critical strip at the rate N^{1/4} e^{-pi sqrt(N)/4}. New in this book.
- [Zeros of the symmetrised finite stages and a sufficient condition for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hurwitz_zeros_of_finite_stages_and_sufficient_condition_for_rh) (Corollary 14.12.2, page 676; proved): By Hurwitz's theorem the zeros of the finite stages converge to the zeros of xi in the open strip, a simple zero on the critical line is approached by exactly one zero of the symmetrised stage, which lies on the line, and if the symmetrised stages have no zeros in the right half of the strip up to heights tending to infinity along some sequence of stages then RH holds. Whether RH implies that hypothesis on the stages is open. New in this book.
- [Finite order GGC, Bondesson and HCM classes of the clock, and RH as the infinite order case](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_order_ggc_bondesson_and_hcm_classes_of_the_clock) (Theorem 14.13.2, page 683; proved): From the verification of RH up to height 3 times 10^12 the clock lies in the finite order GGC and Bondesson classes up to order 1.16 times 10^25 and its Laplace transform is hyperbolically completely monotone up to order 9 times 10^12, while RH is equivalent to the clock being a GGC, to its being in the Bondesson class, and to its transform being hyperbolically completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Finite arithmetic form of the basepoint density below basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_arithmetic_form_of_basepoint_density_below_basepoint_one) (Proposition 14.14.1, page 687; conditional on Part (b) assumes the Riemann hypothesis. Part (a) holds without any hypothesis, and part (c) holds without any hypothesis when delta is at least one half and otherwise needs that every zero lies within delta of the critical line, which the Riemann hypothesis gives for every delta above zero): For basepoint alpha equal to one half plus delta, a Fejér tapered sum over the primes below e^X, two explicit pole terms and one gamma integral define a quantity A_X, which is half the sum over all zeros rho of a function that is nonnegative on the real line, evaluated at (rho minus one half)/i, is nonnegative under RH, and tends to the real part of the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha plus it as X grows when every zero lies within delta of the critical line. New in this book.
- [Zero freeness of the symmetric finite stages of the maximum](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_zero_freeness_of_symmetric_finite_stages_of_the_maximum) (Problem 14.1, page 690; open): Find heights tending to infinity such that, for infinitely many N, the symmetric finite stage of the maximum has no zeros in the right half of the critical strip below that height, for instance heights of order the square root of N; either statement would prove RH. Numerical counts for N up to 96 suggest that the zeros stay on the line up to a height of order N, and a mechanism for that is the first thing to find. New in this book.
- [A termwise positive continuation of the prime form below basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_termwise_positive_continuation_of_prime_form_below_basepoint_one) (Problem 14.2, page 691; open): Is there a continuation of the sine squared prime form of the Thorin density below basepoint one that is positive term by term, for instance through smoothed prime sums with a cutoff near e^{1/epsilon} whose loss can be controlled by the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha, the gamma sum and the pole terms? A positive answer for every basepoint in (alpha_0, 1] would prove the zero free region beta at most alpha_0. New in this book.
- [Existence of the half flow clock for small positive times](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_existence_of_half_flow_clock_for_small_positive_times) (Problem 14.3, page 691; open): For times t between 0 and 0.2, does the law with Laplace transform R_t(lambda/2), half of the clock of the de Bruijn Newman flow, exist as a probability law, and is it infinitely divisible? Unconditionally it is known to exist at t = 0, where it is half the clock, and to exist and be a GGC for t at least 0.2; under RH it exists and is a GGC for every t at least 0. New in this book.
- [An analogue of the Khinchin factorisation at one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_khinchin_analogue_of_tilted_maximum_at_one_half) (Problem 14.4, page 691; open): Is there an analogue at sigma equal to one half of the Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum, that is, a factorisation of the tilted law of the clock or of the Pólya variable through a law built from the primes, with the explicit formula replacing the Euler product? New in this book.

#### Key terms

Pólya density, Polya density, maximum order statistic, maximum of independent exponential variables, Thorin measure, clock, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Khinchin factorisation, zeta distribution, Wald couple, logistic law, Stieltjes criterion, Laplace distance, Gumbel norming constant, Hurwitz theorem, Bondesson class, hyperbolically completely monotone, HCM, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: The Thorin phase diagram
chapters.summary:
Which computations can see past the height to which the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) has been verified, and which comes closest to RH? The chapter answers with the Thorin phase diagram: the GGC region of points $(t,\alpha)$, with $t\ge0$ the time of the de Bruijn Newman heat flow $\xi_t$ and $\alpha\ge\frac12$ a basepoint, at which the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC). It proves a threshold theorem along the flow, which extends the case $t=0$ of Polson (2026) (the clock is a GGC exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ lies to the right of $\alpha$), and the phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form: the region is carried along parabolas by the flow, the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH is the corner $(0,\frac12)$. It sorts the routes of the book into finite information routes and three that reach every height, writes a winding number certificate for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ and runs its finite part in ball arithmetic, computes Thorin densities of $\xi_t$ from the Pólya integral, reports Weil Gram matrix and zero gas experiments, fits the cost of the flow route to the Polymath15 table, and poses five open problems.

#### From the literature

- the strip theorem and $\Lambda\le\frac12$ (de Bruijn 1950), $\Lambda<\frac12$ (Ki, Kim and Lee 2009), the constant $\Lambda$ (Newman 1976), $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- the effective Riemann Siegel type approximation of $H_t$, $\Lambda\le0.22$ and the table of conditional bounds (Polymath 2019); RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ and $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- generalized gamma convolutions and their weak limits (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- Weil's explicit formula and criterion (Weil 1952); Lehmer pairs (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994)
- explicit bounds for $S(T)$ (Backlund 1918; Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); the Biane, Pitman and Yor lattice (2001)
- the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, announced, not refereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Theorems and certified computations are proved, the cost law is conditional on its fitted form, and the problems are open.

- [Threshold theorem along the flow for the shifted clocks of the heat flow function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#threshold_theorem_shifted_clock_along_heat_flow) (Theorem 15.2.3, page 700; proved): For every time $t\ge0$ and basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, the shifted clock of the heat flow function $\xi_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ has real part above $\alpha$, and its Thorin measure is then an explicit sum of Cauchy kernels and atoms over the zeros. New in this book.
- [Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#phase_diagram_theorem_de_bruijn_strip_theorem_in_thorin_form) (Theorem 15.3.2, page 702; proved): The set of points $(t,\alpha)$ where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner $(0,\frac12)$ belongs to it. New in this book.
- [Winding number certificate for the point (0.2, 0.6) of the phase diagram](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#winding_number_certificate_for_point_0_2_0_6_of_phase_diagram) (Theorem 15.5.6, page 708; proved): Given a barrier above which zeros are excluded (Polymath15 provide one; no script of the book checks it), if a ball arithmetic evaluation of $\xi_{0.2}$ on a grid along the left, top and right edges of a rectangle (on the bottom edge, which is real, $\xi_{0.2}$ is positive) satisfies explicit inequalities with an argument sum in $(-\pi,\pi)$, then $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero with real part above $0.6$, so the point $(0.2,0.6)$ lies in the GGC region and $\Lambda\le0.22$. New in this book.
- [Certificate in Thorin form, positive logarithmic derivative on a rectangle excludes zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_form_certificate_positive_log_derivative_on_rectangle) (Proposition 15.5.7, page 709; proved): If, for some $\frac12<\alpha<\sigma_1$ and $T>0$, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of $\xi_t$ is positive at every point $\sigma+i\theta$ of the rectangle $[\alpha,\sigma_1]\times[0,T]$ where $\xi_t$ does not vanish, then $\xi_t$ has no zero with real part in $(\alpha,\sigma_1]$ and ordinate in $(0,T)$. New in this book.
- [No zero of the time 0.2 function in the rectangle up to height 160, certified](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#xi_time_0_2_no_zero_in_rectangle_up_to_height_160_certified) (Theorem 15.5.8, page 711; proved): A computation in ball arithmetic certifies that $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero with real part between $0.6$ and $0.9$ and ordinate between $0$ and $160$, which checks the finite part of the certificate for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ of the phase diagram below height $160$ (the certificate needs it up to the barrier of Polymath15, near height $3\times10^{10}$). New in this book.
- [Pair of zeros near height 185 still real at time minus 0.287979, certified](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_flow_zero_pair_near_height_185_still_real_at_minus_0_287979_certified) (Proposition 15.6.1, page 715; proved): A certified computation in ball arithmetic shows that the pair of zeros of the heat flow function near height $185$ is still real at time $-0.287979$, the upper end of the book's bracket for the time of their collision, and certified signs next to the double zero located by Newton's method lower that end to $-0.287979837008$. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the candidate Thorin densities at times 0 and 0.2 near the Polymath15 barrier](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_thorin_densities_at_time_0_and_0_2_near_polymath15_barrier) (Problem 15.1, page 718; open): Compute the functions $v_t/\pi$ of the heat flow function (the Thorin densities of its shifted clocks where these are generalized gamma convolutions) at $t=0$ and $t=0.2$ at heights near $3\times10^{10}$ and measure how their difference grows with the height. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the boundary of the GGC region for 0 at most t at most 0.2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_boundary_of_ggc_region_for_times_up_to_0_2) (Problem 15.2, page 718; open): Describe the boundary $\alpha^*(t)$ of the GGC region for $0\le t\le0.2$, decide whether it is continuous, and whether $(\alpha^*(t)-\frac12)^2+\frac t2$ is strictly decreasing where $\alpha^*(t)>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Open problem on a coordinate on the phase diagram for the symmetrised truncations](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_phase_diagram_coordinate_for_symmetrised_truncations) (Problem 15.3, page 718; open): Find explicit truncations of the heat flow function, built from finitely many terms without the zeros and converging to it on compact sets, and a point $(t,\alpha)$ outside the known part of the phase diagram such that infinitely many truncations have no zero to the right of $\alpha$ below heights that grow to infinity; Hurwitz's theorem would then add the point to the GGC region. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the Cholesky factor of the Weil Gram matrix](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_cholesky_factor_of_weil_gram_matrix_on_hat_functions) (Problem 15.4, page 719; open): Compute the Cholesky factor of the Weil Gram matrix on hat functions for decreasing width and increasing support, and decide whether its entries converge to an object built from the arithmetic. New in this book.
