Write $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}{f}(\alpha+i\theta)$, let $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ be the digamma function and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and let $q=1$, $4$, $12$ for the three functions in the order above. For $\sigma>1$ and real $\theta$, $v_\sigma(\theta)\ge A^\infty_f(\sigma,\theta)-S_f(\sigma)$, where \[A^\infty_\xi(\sigma,\theta)=-\tfrac12\log\pi+\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\big(\tfrac{\sigma+i\theta}2\big),\quad A^\infty_{\chi_4}(\sigma,\theta)=\tfrac12\log\tfrac4\pi+\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\big(\tfrac{\sigma+1+i\theta}2\big),\quad A^\infty_{\chi_{12}}(\sigma,\theta)=\tfrac12\log\tfrac{12}\pi+\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\big(\tfrac{\sigma+i\theta}2\big),\] and $S_f(\sigma)=\sum_{(n,q)=1}\Lambda(n)n^{-\sigma}$, so that $S_\xi=-\zeta'/\zeta$, $S_{\chi_4}(\sigma)=S_\xi(\sigma)-\log2/(2^\sigma-1)$ and $S_{\chi_{12}}(\sigma)=S_{\chi_4}(\sigma)-\log3/(3^\sigma-1)$; moreover $A^\infty_f(\sigma,\theta)$ increases in $|\theta|$. Hence, if $\frac12<\alpha<\alpha'$ with $\alpha'>1$, $\theta$ is real, and every zero $\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ of $f$ with $\delta>(\alpha-\frac12)/\sqrt2$ satisfies $|\theta-\gamma|\ge(1+\sqrt2)\delta$ (the comparison hypothesis, which holds at every $\theta$ when all zeros of $f$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$, that is under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\xi$ or the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $\chi_4$ or $\chi_{12}$, and at every $\theta$ when $\alpha\ge\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt2}$ with no hypothesis), then \[v_\alpha(\theta)\ \ge\ \frac{\alpha-\frac12}{\alpha'-\frac12}\Big(A^\infty_f(\alpha',\theta)-S_f(\alpha')\Big)\ =\ \frac{\alpha-\frac12}{2\alpha'-1}\log|\theta|+O(1),\] the $O(1)$ being as $|\theta|\to\infty$ with $\alpha$, $\alpha'$ and $f$ fixed.
results.label: cor:dbeta:lower

results.name: Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and its equivalence with RH
results.summary: RH, respectively GRH for the Dirichlet L function of the character modulo 4 or modulo 12, is equivalent to the Thorin density of the corresponding completed function on every line with real part between one half and one being smallest at the origin and only there, a property certified in ball arithmetic with no hypothesis up to the verified height.
results.statement:
Let $f$ be one of $\xi$, $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ and $\xi(\cdot,\chi_{12})$, where $\xi$ is the completed Riemann zeta function and $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ and $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma( rac s2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ are the completed Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal character modulo $4$ and of the real primitive character modulo $12$; each $f$ is entire of order one, real on the real axis, with $f(s)=f(1-s)$ and no real zeros. Write $v_\alpha(	heta)=\operatorname{Re} rac{f'}{f}(\alpha+i	heta)$, $b_\alpha=v_\alpha(0)= rac{f'}{f}(\alpha)$ and $V_f=(\log f)''( rac12)$, which is $0.04620998623$, $0.1560296499$ and $0.3329236082$ for the three functions in the order above. Let $H_0$ be a height below which every zero of $f$ is known to lie on the critical line, $H_0=3	imes10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), $2.5	imes10^7$ and $10^8/12$ (Platt 2016) for the three functions, and let $\alpha_{\max}=7.35$, $4.70$ and $3.10$ for the three functions. Then: (i) for every $\alpha> rac12$, $0<b_\alpha\le(\alpha- rac12)V_f$, and the ratio $b_\alpha/(\alpha- rac12)$ decreases in $\alpha$ and tends to $V_f$ as $\alpha\downarrow rac12$; (ii) for $ rac12<\alpha\le\alpha_{\max}$, $v_\alpha(	heta)>b_\alpha$ for $0<|	heta|\le H_0- rac{1+\sqrt2}2$; (iii) for $ rac12+ rac1{\sqrt2}\le\alpha\le\alpha_{\max}$, $v_\alpha(	heta)>b_\alpha$ for every real $	heta
e0$; (iv) for $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ and $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi_{12})$, $v_\alpha(	heta)>b_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\ge rac12+ rac1{\sqrt2}$ and every real $	heta
e0$; (v) for $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ and $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi_{12})$, $v_\alpha(	heta)>b_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\ge1$ and every real $	heta
e0$; (vi) the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) for $\xi$, respectively the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $\chi_4$ or for $\chi_{12}$ (all zeros of $f$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s= rac12$), holds if and only if $v_\alpha(	heta)>b_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in( rac12,1)$ and every real $	heta
e0$.
results.label: thm:dbeta:minall

results.name: Certified positivity of the heat trace at the basepoint one
results.summary: The heat trace of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is certified positive at every time, with an explicit lower bound, from the primes up to ten million and published explicit bounds for Chebyshev's error, in ball arithmetic.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $v_1(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+i\theta)$, and $T_1$ the generalized gamma convolution with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_1}=\xi(1)/\xi(1+\sqrt u)$. Let $k_1(t)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^\infty e^{-t\theta^2}v_1(\theta)\,d\theta$ for $t>0$ be the heat trace of $T_1$, that is, the Laplace transform in the variable $z=\theta^2$ of its Thorin measure. Then $2\sqrt{\pi t}\,k_1(t)>0.021$ for every $t>0$. The proof uses the primes up to $10^7$, explicit bounds for $\psi(y)-y$, where $\psi(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$ is Chebyshev's function and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function (Büthe 2018; Broadbent, Kadiri, Lumley, Ng and Wilk 2021; Johnston and Yang 2023), and a computation in ball arithmetic.
results.label: bp:prop:heatcert

results.name: No Brownian first passage to a random level at the basepoint one
results.summary: The shifted clock at the basepoint one is not the first passage time of a Brownian motion with drift to a random level independent of the motion.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $T_1$ the generalized gamma convolution with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_1}=\xi(1)/\xi(1+\sqrt u)$. Let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion and, for $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and $a\ge0$, let $H^{(c)}_a=\inf\{t:B_t+ct\ge a\}$ be the first passage time of $B_t+ct$ to the level $a$. For no drift $c\ge0$ and no random level $L\ge0$ independent of the Brownian motion is $T_1$ equal in law to the first passage time $H^{(c)}_L$. (For $c<0$ the first passage time is infinite with positive probability, so equality is impossible.)
results.label: bp:prop:nogo

results.name: Subordination of the tilted centre clock at the basepoint one
results.summary: The shifted clock at the basepoint one is the exponentially tilted centre clock run through the inverse local time of a sticky Brownian motion, equivalently the tilted clock plus a Brownian first passage time to a level proportional to it.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $T$ the centre clock, the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ for $u\ge0$, which exists with no hypothesis on the zeros (its existence uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis below height $1000$). Let $\widetilde T$ have the tilted law $P(\widetilde T\in dt)=e^{-t/4}P(T\in dt)/\mathbb{E}e^{-T/4}$, and let $(\sigma_\ell)_{\ell\ge0}$ be a subordinator independent of $\widetilde T$ with Laplace exponent $u+\sqrt u$, that is, $\mathbb{E}e^{-u\sigma_\ell}=e^{-\ell(u+\sqrt u)}$. Then the shifted clock $T_1$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_1}=\xi(1)/\xi(1+\sqrt u)$, satisfies \[T_1\stackrel{d}{=}\sigma_{\widetilde T}\stackrel{d}{=}\widetilde T+H_{\widetilde T/\sqrt2},\] where $H_a$ is the first passage time of a standard Brownian motion to the level $a$, independent of $\widetilde T$.
results.label: bp:thm:sub

results.name: Kent string hitting time of the shifted clock at the basepoint one under RH
results.status_text: conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis (every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half) and the simplicity of every nontrivial zero
results.conditions: the Riemann Hypothesis (every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half) and the simplicity of every nontrivial zero
results.summary: Assuming RH and simple zeros, the tilted centre clock is a Kent hitting time of a Krein string with spectrum the squared moduli of the zeros, and the shifted clock at the basepoint one is the first hitting time of a level by this string diffusion run on the local time of a sticky Brownian motion.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the centre clock, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$, where $\xi$ is the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\widetilde T$ be the clock tilted by $e^{-t/4}$, $P(\widetilde T\in dt)=e^{-t/4}P(T\in dt)/\mathbb{E}e^{-T/4}$, and let $T_1$ be the shifted clock with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_1}=\xi(1)/\xi(1+\sqrt u)$, so that $T_1\stackrel{d}{=}\sigma_{\widetilde T}$ for an independent subordinator $\sigma$ with Laplace exponent $u+\sqrt u$, the inverse local time at zero of a Brownian motion $B$ that is sticky at zero. Assume RH and that all nontrivial zeros are simple. Then $\widetilde T$ is Kent's hitting time for a Krein string whose Dirichlet spectrum is $\{\gamma^2+\frac14\}=\{|\rho|^2\}$ ($\gamma>0$ running over the ordinates of the zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$), and $T_1$ is the first hitting time of the level $y_*$ by the process $D(\ell_t)$, where $D$ is that string diffusion started at its left end, $y_*$ is the level whose hitting time by $D$ is $\widetilde T$, and $\ell_t$ is the local time at zero of the independent sticky Brownian motion $B$. Equivalently, $T_1$ is the first hitting time of the line $\{y=y_*\}$ by the two dimensional Markov process $(D(\ell_t),B_t)$.
results.label: bp:cor:kent

results.name: Subordination of the centre clock at every basepoint above the centre
results.summary: For every basepoint above the centre the shifted clock exists with no hypothesis on the zeros and is a Brownian hitting time built from the tilted centre clock, with a stable one half tail, and, by the threshold theorem of Polson 2026, it is a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$, and $T$ the centre clock, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$. For every $\alpha>\frac12$, with no hypothesis on the zeros (the existence of the centre clock uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis below height $1000$), $\varphi_\alpha(u)=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of $T_\alpha\stackrel{d}{=}\sigma^{(\alpha)}_{\widetilde T_\alpha}$, where $\widetilde T_\alpha$ is the centre clock tilted by $e^{-(\alpha-\frac12)^2T}$, that is, $P(\widetilde T_\alpha\in dt)=e^{-(\alpha-\frac12)^2t}P(T\in dt)/\mathbb{E}e^{-(\alpha-\frac12)^2T}$, and $\sigma^{(\alpha)}$ is an independent subordinator with exponent $u+2(\alpha-\frac12)\sqrt u$, that is, $T_\alpha\stackrel{d}{=}\widetilde T_\alpha+H_{\sqrt2(\alpha-\frac12)\widetilde T_\alpha}$ with $H_a$ the first passage time of a standard Brownian motion to the level $a$, independent of $\widetilde T_\alpha$. The law has infinite mean and $P(T_\alpha>x)\sim\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)\,(\pi x)^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$. By the threshold theorem of Polson (2026), the variable $T_\alpha$ is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if no zero has $\beta>\alpha$, in particular for every $\alpha\ge1$, and when every zero has $\beta<\alpha$ its Thorin density in the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$ is $\frac1\pi\sum_\rho\frac{\alpha-\beta}{(\alpha-\beta)^2+(\theta-\gamma)^2}$.
results.label: bp:thm:alpha

results.name: Lévy measure and self decomposability of the shifted clock
results.summary: The shifted clock at every basepoint above the centre is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, with an explicit Lévy measure obtained from that of the centre clock.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$, let $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)=\prod_j(1+u/a_j)$ with $a_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, and let $W(x)=\sum_je^{-a_jx}$, so that the centre clock $T$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$, is infinitely divisible with Lévy measure $W(x)\,dx/x$; with no hypothesis on the zeros (using the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis below height $1000$), $W>0$ and $W'<0$ on $(0,\infty)$. Let $\alpha>\frac12$, $a=\alpha-\frac12$, and let $T_\alpha$ be the shifted clock with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$. Then $T_\alpha$ is infinitely divisible, with no drift and Lévy measure $W_\alpha(x)\,dx/x$, where \[W_\alpha(x)=\frac{ax}{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^x(x-s)^{-3/2}e^{-a^2xs/(x-s)}\,W(s)\,ds=\mathbb{E}\Big[(1+4xV)^{-1/2}\,W\Big(\frac x{1+4xV}\Big)\Big],\] with $V=a^2/(2Z^2)$ and $Z$ a standard normal variable. Hence $W_\alpha>0$ and $W_\alpha'<0$ on $(0,\infty)$, so that $T_\alpha$ is self decomposable; and on every interval $(0,x_0]$ on which $W$ is completely monotone, so is $W_\alpha$.
results.label: bp:cor:levyalpha

results.name: Reciprocal Xi function on the real axis as a normal scale mixture
results.summary: For every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric, unimodal, infinitely divisible law with no hypothesis on the zeros, which has a Cauchy tail when $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $b_\alpha=\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$. For $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $T_\alpha$ be the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\lambda T_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros of $\zeta$; $T_{1/2}$ is the centre clock), let $Z$ be a standard normal variable independent of $T_\alpha$, and put $Y_\alpha=\sqrt{2T_\alpha}\,Z$. Then, for every $\alpha\ge\frac12$, the function $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is the characteristic function of $Y_\alpha$, and the law of $Y_\alpha$ is symmetric, unimodal and infinitely divisible, with no hypothesis on the zeros. At the centre its variance is $2\,\mathbb{E}\,T_{1/2}=2\sum_k a_k^{-1}=0.046210$, where $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$ with one zero $\rho_k$ taken from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$. For $\alpha>\frac12$, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)=1-b_\alpha|u|+O(u^2)$ as $u\to0$ (a corner at the origin), so $Y_\alpha$ lies in the domain of attraction of the Cauchy law, and $P(|Y_\alpha|>y)\sim 2b_\alpha/(\pi y)$ as $y\to\infty$.
results.label: sm:prop:cf

results.name: Thorin form of the reciprocal Xi function and the EGGC criterion
results.summary: When every zero of $\zeta$ has real part less than the basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ (always for $\alpha\ge1$), the characteristic function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ has an explicit Thorin form with the positive density $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)/\pi$, and for $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when there is no zero to the right of $\alpha$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ run over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, and for $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $T_\alpha$ be the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\lambda T_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$, let $Z$ be a standard normal variable independent of $T_\alpha$, $Y_\alpha=\sqrt{2T_\alpha}\,Z$, and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\,(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$ for real $\theta$. Recall that a symmetric law is an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) if and only if it is the law of $Z\sqrt{2T'}$ with $T'$ a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) independent of $Z$, where a GGC is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\{-a\lambda-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\lambda/z)\,U(dz)\}$ for a drift $a\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $U$. Let $\alpha\ge1$, or more generally let $\alpha>\frac12$ be such that $\operatorname{Re}\rho<\alpha$ for every zero $\rho$. Then $v_\alpha>0$ and $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)=\exp\{-\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\log(1+u^2/\theta^2)\,v_\alpha(\theta)\,d\theta\}$ for real $u$, so that $T_\alpha$ is a GGC without drift whose Thorin measure is $(v_\alpha(\theta)/\pi)\,d\theta$ under the substitution $z=\theta^2$, and $Y_\alpha$ is a symmetric EGGC. With no hypothesis on the zeros, for $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law of $Y_\alpha$ is an EGGC if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part greater than $\alpha$, and $Y_{1/2}$ is an EGGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds (that centre statement is the earlier rigidity theorem of Polson, 2026, for the centre clock $T_{1/2}$, read through $Y_{1/2}=\sqrt{2T_{1/2}}\,Z$). Under the Riemann Hypothesis, $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+|u|)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+u^2/\gamma^2)^{-1}$, the product over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$, counted with multiplicity, and $Y_{1/2}$ has the law of $\sum_kL_k/\gamma_k$ with independent standard Laplace variables $L_k$ (density $\frac12e^{-|y|}$).
results.label: sm:thm:thorin

results.name: EGGC property of the reciprocal Xi law across the critical strip
results.summary: For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law $Y_\alpha$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$, and with no hypothesis its characteristic function is that of an extended generalised gamma convolution times a remainder $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)$ with $|\log\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)|\le4(|u|+u^2)\log T_0/T_0$, where $T_0\ge2$ is a height up to which all zeros lie on the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ run over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ (with multiplicity), and for $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $T_\alpha$ be the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\lambda T_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$, $Z$ a standard normal variable independent of $T_\alpha$, $Y_\alpha=\sqrt{2T_\alpha}\,Z$ and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\,(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$. Recall that a symmetric law is an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) if and only if it is the law of $Z\sqrt{2T'}$ with $T'$ a generalised gamma convolution independent of $Z$. Let $\frac12<\alpha<1$ and $\varepsilon=\alpha-\frac12$. (1) With no hypothesis on the zeros, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is the characteristic function of the infinitely divisible, symmetric, unimodal law $Y_\alpha$. If every zero has real part less than $\alpha$, then $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)=\exp\{-\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\log(1+u^2/\theta^2)\,v_\alpha(\theta)\,d\theta\}$ holds with the positive density $v_\alpha(\theta)/\pi=\frac1\pi\sum_\rho\frac{\alpha-\beta}{(\alpha-\beta)^2+(\theta-\gamma)^2}$. (2) $Y_\alpha$ is an EGGC if and only if no zero has $\beta>\alpha$, that is, if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. (3) Let $T_0\ge2$ be a height such that all zeros $\rho$ with $0<\gamma\le T_0$ lie on the critical line. Then $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)=\prod_{0<\gamma\le T_0}\frac{\varepsilon^2+\gamma^2}{(\varepsilon+|u|)^2+\gamma^2}\times\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)$, where the finite product, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ with $0<\gamma\le T_0$ (with multiplicity), is the characteristic function of an EGGC with the positive Thorin density $\sum_{0<\gamma\le T_0}[P_\varepsilon(\theta-\gamma)+P_\varepsilon(\theta+\gamma)]$, $P_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon/(\pi(\varepsilon^2+x^2))$, and the remainder satisfies $|\log\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)|\le C(|u|+u^2)\frac{\log T_0}{T_0}$ for an absolute constant $C$ (the proof gives $C=4$).
results.label: sm:thm:strip

results.name: Complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace is equivalent to RH
results.summary: RH holds exactly when the Poisson trace $\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ of the zeros is completely monotone (the same equivalence for the heat trace was shown earlier by Polson 2026), and for $\alpha\ge1$ the corresponding trace is completely monotone with no hypothesis and decays like $b_\alpha/(\pi y)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\rho_k=\beta_k+i\gamma_k$ ($\gamma_k>0$) be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity, and put $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$ and $\sqrt{a_k}=\gamma_k+i(\frac12-\beta_k)$ (the root with positive real part). Define the heat trace $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$ and the Poisson trace $K_{1/2}(y)=\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ for $t,y>0$. For $\alpha\ge1$ put $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\,(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$, $b_\alpha=\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ and $K_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty e^{-\theta y}v_\alpha(\theta)\,d\theta$. Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $K_{1/2}$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$, and if and only if $W$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$ (the equivalence with $W$ is the earlier result of Polson, 2026, which the corollary recalls). For every $\alpha\ge1$, with no hypothesis, $K_\alpha$ is completely monotone and $K_\alpha(y)\sim b_\alpha/(\pi y)$ as $y\to\infty$; consequently the Lévy density $K_\alpha(|y|)/|y|$ of the law with characteristic function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is asymptotic to $b_\alpha/(\pi y^2)$, the Lévy density of the Cauchy component.
results.label: sm:cor:poisson

results.name: Unconditional range of the complete monotonicity conditions of the Poisson trace
results.summary: If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the derivative conditions $(-1)^nK^{(n)}(y)>0$ of the Poisson trace $K$ hold at every $0<y<\pi$ and every order $n<H(\pi-y)$; with $H=3\times10^{12}$ this covers all orders below $4.24\times10^{11}$ for $y\le3$.
results.statement: Let $\rho_k=\beta_k+i\gamma_k$ ($\gamma_k>0$) be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity, $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$, $\sqrt{a_k}=\gamma_k+i\delta_k$ with $\delta_k=\frac12-\beta_k$, $\varphi_k=\arctan(\delta_k/\gamma_k)$, and let $K_{1/2}(y)=\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ be the Poisson trace of the zeros. For $n=0,1,2,\dots$ and $y>0$, $(-1)^nK_{1/2}^{(n)}(y)=\sum_k|\sqrt{a_k}|^n\,e^{-\gamma_ky}\cos(n\varphi_k-\delta_ky)$. Suppose that every zero with $0<\gamma_k\le H$ lies on the critical line. Then for $0<y<\pi$ and every integer $n$ with $0\le n<H(\pi-y)$, every term of this series is positive, and $(-1)^nK_{1/2}^{(n)}(y)>0$. With $H=T_0=3\times10^{12}$, the height up to which Platt and Trudgian verified that all zeros lie on the critical line, this covers all $n<9.12\times10^{12}$ at $y=0.1$, all $n<6.42\times10^{12}$ at $y=1$ and all $n<4.24\times10^{11}$ at $y=3$.
results.label: thm:biane:cmrange

results.name: Positive definite and bounded forms of the Poisson trace criterion for RH
results.summary: RH is equivalent to positive definiteness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ for every $x>0$, and to boundedness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ on $[0,\infty)$ for some $x>0$, where $K_{1/2}$ is the Poisson trace of the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\rho_k=\beta_k+i\gamma_k$ ($\gamma_k>0$) be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity, and put $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$ and $\sqrt{a_k}=\gamma_k+i(\frac12-\beta_k)$. For complex $z$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ let $K_{1/2}(z)=\sum_ke^{-z\sqrt{a_k}}$ (the Poisson trace of the zeros, absolutely and locally uniformly convergent, hence analytic). The following are equivalent: (i) the Riemann Hypothesis; (ii) $K_{1/2}$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$; (iii) for every $x>0$ the function $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ is positive definite on $\mathbb{R}$; (iv) for some $x>0$ the function $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$. Under these conditions $|K_{1/2}(x+iy)|\le K_{1/2}(x)$ for $x>0$ and real $y$.
results.label: prop:biane:pd

results.name: Small y asymptotics of the Poisson trace and Pólya's trace
results.summary: As $y\to0+$ the Poisson trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ and the trace of the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ have the same main term and their difference tends to $\frac98$, with a refined second term under RH.
results.statement: Let $\rho_k=\beta_k+i\gamma_k$ ($\gamma_k>0$) be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity, $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$, $\sqrt{a_k}=\gamma_k+i(\frac12-\beta_k)$, and $K_{1/2}(y)=\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ (the Poisson trace of the zeros). Let $P(\theta)=K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$, with $K_\nu$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind (Pólya's function), let $\theta_1\le\theta_2\le\cdots$ be its positive zeros, counted with multiplicity, and $K^P(y)=\sum_ne^{-\theta_ny}$. Let $\gamma_E$ be Euler's constant, $M(y)=\frac1{2\pi y}\big(\log\frac1{2\pi y}-\gamma_E\big)$ and $c=2\pi-\frac1{6\pi}-\frac1{48\pi}=6.2235022035$. As $y\to0+$: (i) $K_{1/2}(y)=M(y)+\frac78+O(y\log\frac1y)$, and under the Riemann Hypothesis $K_{1/2}(y)=M(y)+\frac78+\frac1{48\pi}y\log\frac1y+o(y\log\frac1y)$; (ii) $K^P(y)=M(y)-\frac14+\big(2\pi-\frac1{6\pi}\big)y\log\frac1y+O(y)$; (iii) $D(y)=K_{1/2}(y)-K^P(y)=\frac98+O(y\log\frac1y)$, and under the Riemann Hypothesis $D(y)=\frac98-c\,y\log\frac1y+o(y\log\frac1y)$.
results.label: prop:biane:traces

results.name: Explicit obstruction and approximation cost for translates of the tilted Pólya kernel
results.summary: For translates of the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ the book proves an explicit obstruction at the centre (no finite combination approximates $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ with $L^1$ error below $\sup_\gamma|\hat g(\gamma)|$, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros on the critical line) and, where the translates are dense, an explicit cost of approximation (a combination within $\delta$ of $g$ has coefficient sum at least $(|\hat g(\gamma)|-\delta)/|\xi(\alpha+i\gamma)|$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$); the density criteria (dense exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; dense for every $\alpha>\frac12$ exactly when RH holds) restate Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932).
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be Pólya's kernel, an even, positive function that decays doubly exponentially and satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{su}\,du=\xi(\frac12+s)$ for every complex $s$. For $\alpha\ge\frac12$ put $\Phi_\alpha(u)=e^{(\alpha-\frac12)u}\Phi(u)$, so that $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_\alpha(u)e^{i\theta u}\,du=\xi(\alpha+i\theta)$, and for $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ put $\hat g(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(u)e^{i\theta u}\,du$. (1) The translates $\Phi_\alpha(\cdot-x)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, span a dense subspace of $L^1(\mathbb{R})$ if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$. (2) At the centre ($\alpha=\frac12$) they are not dense: for every finite combination $h=\sum_kc_k\Phi(\cdot-x_k)$ and every $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, $\|g-h\|_1\ge\sup_\gamma|\hat g(\gamma)|$, the supremum over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line. (3) At the basepoint one they are dense, with no hypothesis on the zeros. (4) For $\alpha_0\in[\frac12,1)$, $\zeta$ has no zeros in the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ if and only if the translates of $\Phi_\alpha$ are dense in $L^1(\mathbb{R})$ for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$; in particular the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if they are dense for every $\alpha>\frac12$. (5) If the translates of $\Phi_\alpha$ are dense, $h=\sum_kc_k\Phi_\alpha(\cdot-x_k)$, $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and $\|g-h\|_1\le\delta$, then $\sum_k|c_k|\ge(|\hat g(\gamma)|-\delta)/|\xi(\alpha+i\gamma)|$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$. Parts (1), (3) and (4) restate Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932) for $\Phi_\alpha$; parts (2) and (5) are what the completeness form adds.
results.label: wr:prop:wiener

results.name: Pólya kernel analogue of Salem's criterion
results.summary: RH holds if and only if, for every $\frac12<\alpha<1$, the convolution equation with the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ has no bounded nonzero solution; at the centre $\cos(\gamma y)$ solves it for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, let $\Phi$ be Pólya's kernel, the even positive function with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{su}\,du=\xi(\frac12+s)$ for every complex $s$, and put $\Phi_\alpha(u)=e^{(\alpha-\frac12)u}\Phi(u)$ and $\Xi(\gamma)=\xi(\frac12+i\gamma)$. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if, for every $\frac12<\alpha<1$, the equation $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_\alpha(x-y)f(y)\,dy=0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ has no bounded solution $f\ne0$. At the centre ($\alpha=\frac12$) the equation has the explicit bounded solutions $f(y)=\cos(\gamma y)$, one for each ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$ on the critical line, because $\Xi(\gamma)=0$ there; at the basepoint one ($\alpha=1$) it has none. Salem (1953) proved the corresponding statement with the Fermi Dirac kernel in place of $\Phi_\alpha$.
results.label: wr:cor:salem

results.name: Twisted Riesz function and the basepoint form of Riesz's criterion
results.summary: Twisting Riesz's function by $(x/n^2)^{ih}$ changes the Gamma factor of its Mellin transform to $\Gamma(1-s+ih)/\zeta(2s)$ and keeps the criterion: $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$ exactly when $R_h(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the Möbius function and, for real $h$ and $x>0$, let $R_h(x)=x\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}{n^2}\big(\frac x{n^2}\big)^{ih}e^{-x/n^2}$; for $h=0$ this is Riesz's function $R(x)=x\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)n^{-2}e^{-x/n^2}=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-x)^k}{(k-1)!\,\zeta(2k)}$. For every real $h$ and $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $\int_0^\infty R_h(x)\,x^{-s-1}\,dx=\Gamma(1-s+ih)/\zeta(2s)$. For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$, $\zeta$ has no zeros in the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$ if and only if $R_h(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ as $x\to\infty$ for every $\delta>0$. In particular the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $R_h(x)=O(x^{1/4+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$. For $h=0$ and $\alpha=\frac12$ this is Riesz's criterion (Riesz 1916).
results.label: ri:prop:twisted

results.name: The Riesz function as an average over the centre clock
results.summary: With no hypothesis, Riesz's function is minus the expectation of an alternating series in the centre clock whose terms decay like $e^{-4k^2T}$ instead of $1/(k-1)!$.
results.statement: Let $R(x)=x\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)n^{-2}e^{-x/n^2}=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-x)^k}{(k-1)!\,\zeta(2k)}$ be Riesz's function ($\mu$ the Möbius function), $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ the completed Riemann zeta function, and $T$ the centre clock, the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\lambda T}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$. For every $x>0$, with no hypothesis on the zeros of $\zeta$, $R(x)=-\frac1{\xi(1/2)}\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{k\ge1}k(2k-1)\Big(-\frac x\pi\Big)^ke^{-(2k-\frac12)^2T}\Big]$, the expectation of the series being the series of the expectations.
results.label: ri:prop:avg

results.name: Riesz coefficients as values of GGC Laplace transforms
results.summary: For $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$, $1/\zeta(2k)$ is an explicit multiple of the Laplace transform of the basepoint clock $T_\alpha$ at $(2k-\alpha)^2$, in particular of the centre clock at $\alpha=\frac12$ and of the basepoint one clock at $\alpha=1$, and at $\alpha=1$ it is $\kappa_k$ times the exponential of minus a Thorin integral, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, and for $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $T_\alpha$ be the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\lambda T_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros). Put $\kappa_k=2k(2k-1)(k-1)!/\pi^k$ and $\rho_{1/2}(\theta)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\,(\xi'/\xi)(1+i\theta)$. For every $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$ and every integer $k\ge1$, $\frac1{\zeta(2k)}=\frac{\kappa_k}{2\xi(\alpha)}\,\mathbb{E}\,e^{-(2k-\alpha)^2T_\alpha}$. In particular, for the centre clock $T_{1/2}$ and the basepoint one clock $T_1$, where $\xi(1)=\frac12$, $\frac1{\zeta(2k)}=\frac{\kappa_k}{2\xi(\frac12)}\,\mathbb{E}\,e^{-(2k-\frac12)^2T_{1/2}}=\kappa_k\,\mathbb{E}\,e^{-(2k-1)^2T_1}$. At $\alpha=1$, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $T_1$ is a generalised gamma convolution without drift whose Thorin measure is $\rho_{1/2}(\theta)\,d\theta$ under the substitution $z=\theta^2$, and $\frac1{\zeta(2k)}=\kappa_k\exp\Big\{-\int_0^\infty\log\Big(1+\frac{(2k-1)^2}{\theta^2}\Big)\rho_{1/2}(\theta)\,d\theta\Big\}$.
results.label: ri:prop:ggccoef

results.name: GGC form of Riesz's criterion
results.summary: Riesz's growth condition at exponent $\alpha/2$ is equivalent to each clock $T_{\alpha'}$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ being a generalised gamma convolution, to positivity of $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)$ on the lines to the right of $\alpha$, and to convergence of a compensated sine squared sum over the primes; for $\alpha=\frac12$, RH holds exactly when every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a GGC.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $R(x)=x\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)n^{-2}e^{-x/n^2}=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-x)^k}{(k-1)!\,\zeta(2k)}$ Riesz's function ($\mu$ the Möbius function), $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\,(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ let $T_\alpha$ be the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, $\lambda\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros); a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\{-a\lambda-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\lambda/z)\,U(dz)\}$ for a drift $a\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $U$. For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent. (1) $R(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ as $x\to\infty$ for every $\delta>0$. (2) $\zeta$ has no zeros with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. (3) $T_{\alpha'}$ is a GGC for every $\alpha'>\alpha$. (4) For every $\alpha'>\alpha$, $v_{\alpha'}(\theta)\ge0$ at every real $\theta$ for which $\alpha'+i\theta$ is not a zero of $\xi$. (5) For every $\alpha'>\alpha$ and every real $\theta$ the limit $\lim_{L\to\infty}\Big[\sum_{\log n\le L}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{\alpha'}}\,2\sin^2\big(\tfrac12\theta\log n\big)-\int_0^L2\sin^2\big(\tfrac12\theta x\big)\,e^{(1-\alpha')x}\,dx\Big]$ exists. In particular ($\alpha=\frac12$) the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $T_\alpha$ is a GGC for every $\alpha>\frac12$. For $\alpha=\frac12$ the equivalence of (1) and (2) is Riesz's criterion (Riesz 1916), and that of (2) and (4) is Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999), whose argument gives the equivalence of (2) and (4) for every $\alpha$.
results.label: ri:thm:ggcriesz

results.name: Closed form constant of the squarefree reciprocal sum over number fields
results.summary: Over a number field $K$ of degree $n\ge2$ the sum of $\mu(\mathfrak a)^2/N(\mathfrak a)$ over the integral ideals of norm at most $x$ equals $\frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}(\log x+C_K)+O(x^{-1/n}\log x)$ with the explicit constant $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$, $\gamma_K$ the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n\ge2$ with Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$, let $c_K=\lim_{s\to1}(s-1)\zeta_K(s)$, let $\gamma_K$ be its Euler Kronecker constant, defined by $\zeta_K(s)=c_K/(s-1)+c_K\gamma_K+O(s-1)$, and put $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$. Then, as $x\to\infty$, $\sum_{N(\mathfrak a)\le x}\frac{\mu(\mathfrak a)^2}{N(\mathfrak a)}=\frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}\big(\log x+C_K\big)+O\big(x^{-1/n}\log x\big)$, the sum running over the integral ideals $\mathfrak a$ of $K$ ($\mu$ the Möbius function of ideals, $N$ the norm).
results.label: prop:sqfree:alpha1

results.name: Squarefree Dirichlet series as a gamma factor times a ratio of Pólya moment generating functions
results.summary: The squarefree Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$ equals an explicit gamma factor times $\mathbb{E}\,e^{(s-1/2)X}/\mathbb{E}\,e^{(2s-1/2)X}$ for the Pólya variable $X$, which continues the series to every $s$ with $\xi(2s)\ne0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, let $\Phi$ be Pólya's kernel, the even positive function with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{su}\,du=\xi(\frac12+s)$ for every complex $s$, and let $X$ be the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, so that $\mathbb{E}\,e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ for all complex $s$. Put $\Gamma_{\mathrm{sq}}(s)=\frac{2s-1}{s-1}\,2^s\pi^{-(s+1)/2}\,\Gamma\big(\frac{s+1}2\big)$. For every $s$ with $\xi(2s)\ne0$, $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)^2}{n^s}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{sq}}(s)\,\frac{\mathbb{E}\,e^{(s-\frac12)X}}{\mathbb{E}\,e^{(2s-\frac12)X}}$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and the left side is read as the continuation $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$ where the series diverges.
results.label: prop:sqfree:polya

results.name: Squarefree constant as a combination of two tilted Pólya means
results.summary: The constant $C$ of the squarefree reciprocal sum is an elementary part plus $b_1-2b_2$, a combination of the means of the Pólya variable tilted at the basepoints one and two, which is an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $b_\alpha=\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ (the mean of the Pólya variable $V_\alpha$ tilted to the basepoint $\alpha$, with $\mathbb{E}\,e^{sV_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha+s)/\xi(\alpha)$), $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$ with one zero $\rho_k$ taken from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$, $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$, and let $\gamma_E$ be Euler's constant. The constant $C=\gamma_E-2\zeta'(2)/\zeta(2)$ of $\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)^2/n=\frac6{\pi^2}(\log x+C)+O(x^{-1/2})$ equals $2+\log2-\frac12\log\pi-\frac12\gamma_E+b_1-2b_2$. With no hypothesis on the zeros, $b_1-2b_2=\frac{G'}G\big(\frac14\big)-6\,\frac{G'}G\big(\frac94\big)=\sum_k\Big(\frac1{\frac14+a_k}-\frac6{\frac94+a_k}\Big)=\int_0^\infty\big(e^{-t/4}-6e^{-9t/4}\big)\,W(t)\,dt$, the sum running over the pairs $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ and converging absolutely. Under the Riemann Hypothesis, $a_k=\gamma_k^2$ and $b_1-2b_2=\int\big((z+\frac14)^{-1}-6(z+\frac94)^{-1}\big)\,U_{\mathrm{RH}}(dz)$, where $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ (over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, with multiplicity) is the Thorin measure of the clock $1/G$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:const

results.name: Dedekind zeta clock is a GGC if and only if RH holds for the field
results.summary: For a number field $K$ with $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$, the reciprocal of the normalised completed Dedekind function is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_K$ lie on the critical line, with Thorin measure the sum of point masses at the squared ordinates; this is the number field form of the rigidity theorem of Polson 2026.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ pairs of complex embeddings and discriminant $d_K$, let $\zeta_K$ be its Dedekind zeta function, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, and $\xi_K(s)=s(s-1)\,|d_K|^{s/2}\,\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\,\zeta_K(s)$, an entire function of order one with $\xi_K(s)=\xi_K(1-s)$ whose zeros are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_K$. Suppose $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$ and let $G_K(u)=\xi_K(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi_K(\frac12)$. Then $1/G_K$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution if and only if every zero of $\zeta_K$ in the critical strip lies on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$ (the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$). Its drift is then $0$ and its Thorin measure is $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros counted with multiplicity. This is the number field form of the rigidity theorem of Polson, 2026, with the same proof. A real zero $\beta\in(\frac12,1)$ of $\zeta_K$ would be a pole of $1/G_K$ at the point $(\beta-\frac12)^2$ of the positive axis.
results.label: prop:sqfree:thorinK

results.name: Squarefree constant of a number field through the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function
results.summary: For a number field $K$ the constant $C_K$ is an explicit elementary term $A_K$ plus an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function, and under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$ that sum is a combination of two Stieltjes transform values of the Thorin measure.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ pairs of complex embeddings and discriminant $d_K$, with Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$, residue $c_K=\lim_{s\to1}(s-1)\zeta_K(s)$ and Euler Kronecker constant $\gamma_K$ (defined by $\zeta_K(s)=c_K/(s-1)+c_K\gamma_K+O(s-1)$), and put $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$. Let $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$ and $\xi_K(s)=s(s-1)\,|d_K|^{s/2}\,\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\,\zeta_K(s)$, and let $\gamma_E$ be Euler's constant and $A_K=2+\frac12\log|d_K|+r_1\big(\log2-\frac12\log\pi-\frac12\gamma_E\big)+r_2\big(2-\gamma_E-\log2\pi\big)$. Then $C_K=A_K+\frac{\xi_K'}{\xi_K}(1)-2\,\frac{\xi_K'}{\xi_K}(2)=A_K+\sum_k\Big(\frac1{\frac14+a_{K,k}}-\frac6{\frac94+a_{K,k}}\Big)$, the sum running over the pairs $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi_K$, with multiplicity, where $a_{K,k}=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$ and a zero of order $2m$ at $s=\frac12$ counts as $m$ pairs with $a_{K,k}=0$. Under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$ and $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$, the zero part is $\frac{G_K'}{G_K}\big(\frac14\big)-6\,\frac{G_K'}{G_K}\big(\frac94\big)$ with $G_K(u)=\xi_K(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi_K(\frac12)$, the same combination of values of the Stieltjes transform of the Thorin measure $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ of $1/G_K$ as over $\mathbb{Q}$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:constK

results.name: Exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree counts are equivalent to RH
results.summary: RH holds if and only if the squarefree count smoothed by an exponential law, or by a Gamma(2) law, with mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and under RH with simple zeros an explicit formula with exponentially damped terms at the zeros holds.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the Möbius function, and for $x>0$ let $Q_1(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2e^{-n/x}$ and $Q_2(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2\big(1+\frac{2n}x\big)e^{-2n/x}$, the number of squarefree integers up to a random point of mean $x$ with the exponential law and with the Gamma(2) law respectively. (i) The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $Q_1(x)=\frac6{\pi^2}x+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ as $x\to\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and if and only if $Q_2(x)=\frac6{\pi^2}x+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. (ii) Under the Riemann Hypothesis, if the zeros are simple, $Q_1(x)=\frac6{\pi^2}x+1+\sum_\rho A_\rho x^{\rho/2}+\frac{c_1\log x+c_2}x+O(x^{-2})$ and $Q_2(x)=\frac6{\pi^2}x+1+\sum_\rho B_\rho x^{\rho/2}+\frac{2c_1}x+O(x^{-2})$, where $A_\rho=\frac{\Gamma(\rho/2)\,\zeta(\rho/2)}{2\zeta'(\rho)}$, $B_\rho=\big(1+\frac\rho2\big)\frac{2^{-\rho/2}\,\Gamma(\rho/2)\,\zeta(\rho/2)}{2\zeta'(\rho)}$, the sums over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ are taken over $|\operatorname{Im}\rho|<2T_j$ along a sequence $T_j\to\infty$, $c_1=-\frac{\zeta(-1)}{2\zeta'(-2)}=-1.36843277762021$ and $c_2=c_1\big(1-\gamma_E+\frac{\zeta'(-1)}{\zeta(-1)}-\frac{\zeta''(-2)}{\zeta'(-2)}\big)=-0.339381226129599$, with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant.
results.label: thm:sqfree:smooth

results.name: Lower bound for the squarefree error of the order of the fourth root of x
results.summary: With no hypothesis the squarefree error $\Delta(x)$ satisfies $\limsup\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge0.1004$ and $\liminf\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-0.1004$, so the order $x^{1/4}$ cannot be lowered, and the Gamma(2) smoothed error has the same property with constant $9.94\times10^{-5}$.
results.statement: Let $Q(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)^2$ be the number of squarefree integers up to $x$ and $\Delta(x)=Q(x)-\frac6{\pi^2}x$. Let $\rho_1$ be the zero of $\zeta$ with least positive imaginary part, and $R_{\rho_1}=\frac{\zeta(\rho_1/2)}{\rho_1\zeta'(\rho_1)}$, so that $|R_{\rho_1}|=0.100404$. With no hypothesis, $\limsup_{x\to\infty}\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge|R_{\rho_1}|$ and $\liminf_{x\to\infty}\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-|R_{\rho_1}|$. The same holds for $Q_2(x)-\frac6{\pi^2}x-1$, where $Q_2(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2\big(1+\frac{2n}x\big)e^{-2n/x}$ is the squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$, with $|B_{\rho_1}|=9.944\times10^{-5}$ in place of $|R_{\rho_1}|$, where $B_\rho=\big(1+\frac\rho2\big)\frac{2^{-\rho/2}\,\Gamma(\rho/2)\,\zeta(\rho/2)}{2\zeta'(\rho)}$.
results.label: cor:sqfree:omega

results.name: Squarefree count at a Gamma(n) random point under RH
results.summary: Under RH, the expected squarefree count at a Gamma($n$) random point of mean $x$ is $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}n^{1/8+\varepsilon})$, uniformly in $n\ge1$.
results.statement: Let $Q(x)=\sum_{m\le x}\mu(m)^2$ be the number of squarefree integers up to $x$, and for $n\ge1$ let $G_{n,x}$ have the Gamma($n$) law with mean $x$ (shape $n$, rate $n/x$). Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and uniformly in $n\ge1$, $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_{n,x})=\frac6{\pi^2}\,x+O_\varepsilon\big(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}\,n^{1/8+\varepsilon}\big)$ as $x\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:sqfree:gamman

results.name: Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as a positive average of the Mertens function
results.summary: The squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2$ minus half the expected Mertens function at the random point $\sqrt{x\mathcal{V}_2/2}$, where the density $f_2$ of $\mathcal{V}_2$ is explicit and positive by Lazarević's inequality.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the Möbius function, $M(t)=\sum_{d\le t}\mu(d)$ the Mertens function, and $Q_2(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2\big(1+\frac{2n}x\big)e^{-2n/x}$, the squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$. For $y>0$ let $g_2(y)=\frac2y-\frac1{e^y-1}-\frac y{4\sinh^2(y/2)}$ and $f_2(y)=-2g_2'(y)=\frac4{y^2}-\frac{y\cosh(y/2)}{2\sinh^3(y/2)}$. Then $f_2>0$ (this is Lazarević's inequality $(\sinh z/z)^3>\cosh z$ with $z=y/2$), $f_2(y)=y^2/60+O(y^4)$ as $y\to0$ and $f_2(y)\sim4/y^2$ as $y\to\infty$, and $f_2$ is the density of a probability law $\mathcal{V}_2$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $P(\mathcal{V}_2\ge y)=2g_2(y)$ and $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{V}_2^s=-2\,\Gamma(s+2)\,\zeta(s)$ for $-3<\operatorname{Re}s<1$. For every $x>0$, $Q_2(x)=\frac6{\pi^2}\,x-\frac12\,\mathbb{E}\,M\Big(\sqrt{x\mathcal{V}_2/2}\Big)$. Moreover $f_2$ is twice the difference between the continuous and the integer mixtures of the Gamma(2) densities $\gamma_{2,\lambda}(y)=\lambda^2ye^{-\lambda y}$ over their rate: $f_2(y)=2\Big(\int_0^\infty\gamma_{2,\lambda}(y)\,d\lambda-\sum_{m\ge1}\gamma_{2,m}(y)\Big)$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:mertens

results.name: Gamma smoothing threshold, shape two
results.summary: The signed density that mixes the Mertens function in the Gamma($\nu$) smoothed squarefree error is nonnegative exactly for the shapes $\nu\in(0,2]$, the obstruction above two being the trivial zero of $\zeta$ at $-2$.
results.statement:
Let $\mu$ be the Möbius function, $Q(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)^2$ the number of squarefree integers up to $x$ and $M(t)=\sum_{d\le t}\mu(d)$ the Mertens function. For a shape $
u>0$ let $R_
u(y)= rac{y^{
u+1}}{\Gamma(
u+1)}\sum_{m\ge1}m^
u e^{-my}$, the right Riemann sum with step $y$ of the Gamma($
u+1$) density, and $f_
u(y)= rac{2
u\,(1-R_
u(y))}{y^2}$ for $y>0$. The function $f_
u$ is a signed density of total mass $1$, and for $Y$ with the Gamma($
u$) law of rate $\lambda$, $\mathbb{E}\,Q(Y)= rac6{\pi^2}\,\mathbb{E}\,Y- rac12\int_0^\infty M ig(\sqrt{y/\lambda} ig)f_
u(y)\,dy$. Then $\{
u>0:\ f_
u(y)\ge0	ext{ for all }y>0\}=(0,2]$. Thus two is the largest shape for which the gamma smoothed squarefree error is a positive average of the Mertens function, and the obstruction is the trivial zero of $\zeta$ at $-2$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:threshold

results.name: Pointwise bound for the squarefree error under RH (open)
results.summary: The book asks for a proof, under RH, that the squarefree count has error $O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$, and records forms equivalent to it or sufficient for it.
results.statement: Let $Q(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)^2$ be the number of squarefree integers up to $x$ and $\Delta(x)=Q(x)-\frac6{\pi^2}x$. Open question: prove, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that $\Delta(x)=O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ (by the book, the order $x^{1/4}$ cannot be lowered, and under the Riemann Hypothesis the best bound proved there is $O(x^{2/5+\varepsilon})$, weaker than known conditional exponents such as $7/22$ (Baker and Pintz 1985)). The book gives these forms: remove the loss $n^{1/8}$ from the bound $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_{n,x})=\frac6{\pi^2}x+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}n^{1/8+\varepsilon})$ valid under the Riemann Hypothesis for the count at a Gamma($n$) random point $G_{n,x}$ of mean $x$ (the conjecture implies the bound with no loss, and a loss $n^\delta$ in place of $n^{1/8}$ would give $\Delta(x)=O(x^{1-3/(8\delta+4)+\varepsilon})$, whose exponent tends to $\frac14$ as $\delta\to0$); or show that for large $X$ no $x\in[X,2X]$ has $|\Delta(x)|>CX^{1/4+\varepsilon}$, for some constant $C$ (under the Riemann Hypothesis the book shows that for $C=1$ the set of such $x$ has measure $O(X^{1-\varepsilon})$), which would follow from a bound $O(X^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for the oscillation of $\Delta$ on the subintervals of $[X,2X]$ of length $X^{1-\varepsilon/2}$.
results.label: q:sqfree:pointwise

results.name: Sharpening the lower bound constant for the squarefree error (open)
results.summary: The book asks whether a Fejér kernel over many zeros improves the constant $0.1004$ in the lower bound for the squarefree error, and whether $\limsup|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}$ is infinite.
results.statement: Let $Q(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)^2$ be the number of squarefree integers up to $x$, $\Delta(x)=Q(x)-\frac6{\pi^2}x$, $\rho_1$ the zero of $\zeta$ with least positive imaginary part and $R_{\rho_1}=\frac{\zeta(\rho_1/2)}{\rho_1\zeta'(\rho_1)}$, so that $|R_{\rho_1}|=0.1004$ (to four digits) and, by the book, $\limsup\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge|R_{\rho_1}|$ and $\liminf\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-|R_{\rho_1}|$ with no hypothesis. Open questions: sharpen the constant $|R_{\rho_1}|$ by using many zeros at once with a Fejér kernel, as Ingham did for the Mertens function, and compare it with the observed $\max|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}$, about $1$ for $x$ up to $2\times10^8$; and decide whether $\limsup|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}=\infty$, as the linear independence of the ordinates of the zeros would suggest.
results.label: q:sqfree:fejer

results.name: Background driving subordinator of the centre clock
results.summary: With no hypothesis the centre clock is the integral of $e^{-t}$ against a subordinator whose Lévy density is minus the derivative of the heat trace of the zeros, and RH holds if and only if that density is completely monotone.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function and $G(u)=\xi(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac{1}{2})$. The centre clock $T$ is the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$, $u\ge0$. Let $W(t)=\sum_k e^{-a_kt}$, $t>0$, be the heat trace of the zeros, where $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac{1}{2})^2$ and $\rho_k$ runs over the zeros of $\xi$ with positive imaginary part, counted with multiplicity; under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), $W(t)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-\gamma^2t}$ with $\gamma$ the ordinates of the zeros. With no hypothesis (the proof rests on the inequalities $W>0$ and $W'<0$, whose proof uses only the verification of RH below height $1000$), $T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t$ for a subordinator $Z$ with Lévy density $h(x)=-W'(x)$, which is $\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^2e^{-\gamma^2x}$ under RH and is given for every $x>0$ by the derivative of Weil's explicit formula for $W$ with the test function $e^{-tr^2}$. The condition $\mathbb{E}\log(1+Z_1)<\infty$ holds because $h$ decays exponentially. Moreover RH holds if and only if $h$ is completely monotone.
results.label: sb:prop:bdlp

results.name: Unimodality of the centre clock and the shifted clocks
results.summary: The centre clock and every shifted clock with basepoint above one half have unimodal laws, with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function. The centre clock $T$ is the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\frac{1}{2})/\xi(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{u})$, and for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ is the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$. With no hypothesis, the law of $T$ is unimodal, and so is the law of $T_\alpha$ for every $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$. Here a law is unimodal if its distribution function is convex to the left of some point, a mode, and concave to the right of it.
results.label: sb:cor:unimodal

results.name: The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one is not quasi infinitely divisible
results.summary: The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one, with moment generating function $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$, is not quasi infinitely divisible, hence not infinitely divisible.
results.statement:
Let $\xi(s)= rac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function and let $V_1$ be the tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one, the random variable with moment generating function $\mathbb{E}e^{sV_1}=\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$ (the Esscher tilt by $e^{x/2}$ of the Pólya variable $X$, which has $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi( rac{1}{2}+s)/\xi( rac{1}{2})$). A law is quasi infinitely divisible if its characteristic function is the quotient of two infinitely divisible characteristic functions, equivalently if it has a Lévy Khintchine form with a signed Lévy measure $
u^+-
u^-$ in which $
u^+$ and $
u^-$ are both Lévy measures. Then $V_1$ is not quasi infinitely divisible, and so, an infinitely divisible law being quasi infinitely divisible, it is not infinitely divisible. The reflection $x\mapsto-x$ of the measure $\Pi_1(dx)= ig(e^{-3x}(1-e^{-2x})^{-1}-1 ig)\,dx/x+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)(n\log n)^{-1}\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, is the candidate signed Lévy measure of $V_1$; its pole term $-dx/x$ and its prime atoms at $\log n$ each have infinite mass on $(1,\infty)$, so its positive part and its negative part both have infinite mass there, and its Lévy form converges only as a compensated limit, which exists by the prime number theorem.
results.label: sb:prop:qid

results.name: Thorin Bernstein form of the shifted clock criterion
results.summary: The Laplace exponent of the shifted clock is a Thorin Bernstein function with no hypothesis when the basepoint is at least one, and for basepoints between one half and one exactly when zeta has no zero to the right of the basepoint, while the exponent of the centre clock is one if and only if RH holds.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $G(u)=\xi(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac{1}{2})$ and, for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$, $f_\alpha(u)=u+2(\alpha-\frac{1}{2})\sqrt{u}$. A Thorin Bernstein function is the Laplace exponent of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), equivalently a Bernstein function whose derivative is a Stieltjes function. For every $\alpha\ge1$ the composition $\log G\big((\alpha-\frac{1}{2})^2+f_\alpha(u)\big)-\log G\big((\alpha-\frac{1}{2})^2\big)$, which is the Laplace exponent of the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ (the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$), is a Thorin Bernstein function of $u$ with no hypothesis, while $\log G$ itself, the Laplace exponent of the centre clock, is a Thorin Bernstein function if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds. For $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<1$ the composition is a Thorin Bernstein function if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part greater than $\alpha$.
results.label: sb:prop:tbf

results.name: Upsilon image and free counterpart of the centre clock
results.summary: With no hypothesis the Upsilon image of the centre clock is a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin measure and its Bercovici Pata counterpart is a freely self decomposable unimodal law carried by a half line $[c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, and RH holds if and only if the clock is itself the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $G(u)=\xi(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac{1}{2})=\prod_k(1+u/a_k)$ with $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac{1}{2})^2$, where $\rho_k$ runs over the zeros of $\xi$ with positive imaginary part, counted with multiplicity, and let $T$ be the centre clock, the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$. Put $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$, $h=-W'$, $m_n=\frac{1}{n!}\int_0^\infty t^nW(t)\,dt=\sum_ka_k^{-n-1}$, let $\gamma_1=14.1347\ldots$ be the least ordinate of a zero and $N(\theta)$ the number of zeros with ordinate in $(0,\theta]$. With no hypothesis $T$ is infinitely divisible with no drift and Lévy measure $W(t)\,dt/t$, and self decomposable (because $W>0$ and $W'<0$ on $(0,\infty)$). For a law $\mu$ on $[0,\infty)$ write $\Psi_\mu(s)=-\log\int e^{-sx}\mu(dx)$ for its Laplace exponent. A generalised gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with $\Psi(s)=ds+\int\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)$ for a drift $d\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $U$, and BO is the class of infinitely divisible laws on $[0,\infty)$ with a completely monotone Lévy density. The Upsilon transform $\Upsilon$ maps an infinitely divisible law $\mu$, the law of $X_1$ for a Lévy process $X$, to the law of $\int_0^1\log(1/t)\,dX_t$. The Bercovici Pata bijection $\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}$ maps an infinitely divisible law to the freely infinitely divisible law with the same Lévy Khintchine triplet; $G_\mu(z)=\int\mu(dx)/(z-x)$ is the Cauchy transform of $\mu$ and $\mathcal{C}_\mu(z)=z\varphi_\mu(1/z)$ its free cumulant transform, with $\varphi_\mu$ the Voiculescu transform. A freely infinitely divisible law $\mu$ is free regular if its free convolution powers $\mu^{\boxplus t}$ are carried by $[0,\infty)$ for every $t>0$ (these are the images under $\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}$ of the infinitely divisible laws on $[0,\infty)$). (a) With no hypothesis, $\Upsilon(T)$ is a GGC with no drift and Thorin measure $\widetilde{U}(du)=u^{-2}h(1/u)\,du$, so that $\widetilde{U}((0,u])=W(1/u)>0$ for every $u>0$. Its Laplace exponent is $\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}(s)=\int_0^\infty\log G(sx)\,e^{-x}\,dx=\sum_ke^{a_k/s}E_1(a_k/s)$, $s>0$, with the principal branch of the exponential integral $E_1$; its Lévy density is the completely monotone function $\ell(z)=z^{-1}\int_0^\infty W(z/w)\,e^{-w}\,dw$; its cumulants are $\kappa_n(\Upsilon(T))=n!\,(n-1)!\,m_{n-1}$; and $\int u^{-n}\,\widetilde{U}(du)=n!\,m_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$. Moreover $\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda\Upsilon(T)}=\infty$ for every $\lambda>0$, while $\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda T}<\infty$ exactly when $\lambda<\gamma_1^2$. (b) With no hypothesis, $\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)$ is free regular, freely self decomposable (for every $c\in(0,1)$ it is the free convolution of its dilation by $c$ with some law) and unimodal. Its free cumulant transform is $\mathcal{C}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)}(z)=\int_0^\infty zW(x)/(1-zx)\,dx$, $z\in\mathbb{C}^-$ (the lower half plane), where the right side continues it analytically to $\mathbb{C}\setminus(0,\infty)$, with $\mathcal{C}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)}(-s)=-\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}(s)$ for $s>0$; its free cumulants are $(n-1)!\,m_{n-1}$, the cumulants of $T$. Its Cauchy transform $G_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)}$ satisfies $\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}\big(-G_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)}(z)\big)=1-z\,G_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{BP}}(T)}(z)$ for $z\in\mathbb{C}^+$ (the upper half plane), where $\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}$ is continued analytically to $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0)$ by $\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}(s)=\int_0^\infty sW(y)/(1+sy)\,dy$, and its support lies in $[c,\infty)$, where $c=\max_{s>0}(\Psi_{\Upsilon(T)}(s)-1)/s>0$. (c) RH holds if and only if $T$ is the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law on $[0,\infty)$. In that case $T=\Upsilon(\mu_0)$, where $\mu_0$ is the self decomposable law with no drift and Lévy measure $N(x^{-1/2})\,dx/x$ (canonical function $N(v^{-1/2})$); $\mu_0$ is neither a GGC nor in BO. With no hypothesis, $T$ is not the Upsilon image of a law in BO.
results.label: thm:wigfree:clock

results.name: Peeling a gamma layer from the Pólya generating function keeps zeros real under RH
results.summary: If RH holds, dividing the Taylor coefficients of the Pólya generating function by $(a)_k$ keeps all zeros real and negative for every $a>0$, whereas multiplying the coefficients of a polynomial by $(a)_k$ need not preserve real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function and $G(u)=\xi(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac{1}{2})=\sum_{k\ge0}b_ku^k$, so that the Pólya variable $X$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=G(s^2)$, has $b_k=\mathbb{E}X^{2k}/(2k)!$. For $a>0$ let $(a)_k=a(a+1)\cdots(a+k-1)$ and $G_a(u)=\sum_{k\ge0}b_ku^k/(a)_k$. If the Riemann Hypothesis holds, then for every $a>0$ the function $G_a$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class (the real entire functions that are locally uniform limits of real polynomials with only real zeros) with only real negative zeros, and all its Jensen polynomials $\sum_{i=0}^{d}\binom{d}{i}(n+i)!\,b_{n+i}x^i/(a)_{n+i}$, $d,n\ge0$, have only real negative zeros. Multiplying the coefficients by $(a)_k$ instead does not preserve real zeros: it turns $(1+u)^2=1+2u+u^2$ into $1+2au+a(a+1)u^2$, whose discriminant is $-4a<0$.
results.label: prop:wigfree:peel

results.name: No gamma scale mixture for the Pólya variable and Williams' variable
results.summary: For no shape $a>0$ is the absolute value of the Pólya variable, its square or Williams' variable $S_2$ a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function. The Pólya variable $X$ is the real random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac{1}{2}+s)/\xi(\frac{1}{2})$, $s\in\mathbb{C}$, and Williams' variable $S_2$ is the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda S_2}=\big(\sqrt{2\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{2\lambda}\big)^2$, $\lambda\ge0$ (the sum of two independent hitting times of the level one by a three dimensional Bessel process), for which $\mathbb{E}(\frac{\pi}{2}S_2)^{s/2}=2\xi(s)$. A law is a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws if it is the law of $\Theta\,\Gamma$ with $\Gamma$ gamma distributed with shape $a$ and unit scale and independent of a random variable $\Theta\ge0$. Then for no $a>0$ is $|X|$, $X^2$ or $S_2$ a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws.
results.label: thm:wigfree:nomix

results.name: Thorin measure of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one
results.summary: For the L function of the real character modulo 12, the reciprocal completed function at the basepoint one is the Laplace transform of a GGC with an explicit positive Thorin density, with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{12}$ be the real primitive even Dirichlet character modulo $12$ ($\chi_{12}(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1$ and $-1$ for $n\equiv\pm5 \pmod{12}$, and $0$ if $\gcd(n,12)>1$), $L(s,\chi_{12})$ its Dirichlet $L$ function and $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(s/2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ the completed function, which is entire (there is no pole to remove) and satisfies $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=\xi(1-s,\chi_{12})$. Put $v_1(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+i\theta,\chi_{12})$. Then $\varphi_1(u)=\xi(1,\chi_{12})/\xi(1+\sqrt{u},\chi_{12})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with no drift, whose Thorin measure, in the variable $\theta=\sqrt{z}$, has the density $\frac{1}{\pi}v_1(\theta)=\frac{1}{\pi}\sum_\rho\frac{1-\beta}{(1-\beta)^2+(\theta-\gamma)^2}>0$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi_{12})$, in conjugate pairs. Positivity is unconditional because $L(1+it,\chi_{12})\ne0$ for real $t$.
results.label: bp:eta:prop:thorin

results.name: Lévy form of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one
results.summary: For the completed L function of the real character modulo 12, the logarithm of $\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})/\xi(1,\chi_{12})$ has an explicit Lévy form, with a positive gamma density and prime atoms of both signs, that needs no compensation by a pole term.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{12}$ be the real primitive even Dirichlet character modulo $12$ ($\chi_{12}(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1$ and $-1$ for $n\equiv\pm5 \pmod{12}$, and $0$ if $\gcd(n,12)>1$), $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(s/2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ the completed function of its Dirichlet $L$ function, $b_1=(\xi'/\xi)(1,\chi_{12})$ (which equals $\sum_\rho\rho^{-1}$ over the nontrivial zeros and is $0.1650833123$), $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $\Lambda_{\chi_{12}}(n)=\chi_{12}(n)\Lambda(n)$. For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $\log\frac{\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})}{\xi(1,\chi_{12})}=b_1s+\int_0^\infty(e^{-sx}-1+sx)\,\Pi(dx)$, where $\Pi(dx)=\frac{e^{-x}}{x(1-e^{-2x})}\,dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_{\chi_{12}}(n)}{n\log n}\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, the prime sum converging conditionally, as a limit over $n\le X$ as $X\to\infty$.
results.label: bp:eta:prop:levy

results.name: Almost GGC theorem for the shifted clocks
results.summary: With no hypothesis, for every basepoint between one half and one the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of the basepoint carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the kernels of the other zeros, with a power saving from zero density estimates.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$), counted with multiplicity, let $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$ for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ and let $P_w(x)=w/(\pi(w^2+x^2))$ be the Cauchy kernel of width $w>0$, with $P_0$ the unit point mass at $0$. Write $v_\alpha=v_\alpha^+-v_\alpha^-$ with $v_\alpha^+(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta+\gamma)]$ and $v_\alpha^-(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta+\gamma)]$ (a zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ contributes a unit atom at its ordinate to the positive part), and put $m_\alpha^\pm(T)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^Tv_\alpha^\pm(\theta)\,d\theta$. Recall that the shifted clock $T_\alpha$, with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$, is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when no zero has $\beta>\alpha$, that is when $v_\alpha^-\equiv0$. For every $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<1$, with no hypothesis, $m_\alpha^-(T)/m_\alpha^+(T)\le T^{e(\alpha)-1+o(1)}$ as $T\to\infty$, where $e(\alpha)=3(1-\alpha)/(2-\alpha)$ for $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<\frac{7}{10}$ and $e(\alpha)=15(1-\alpha)/(3+5\alpha)$ for $\frac{7}{10}\le\alpha<1$, and $e(\alpha)<1$ throughout; so the negative part $v_\alpha^-/\pi$, the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of $\alpha$, carries on $[0,T]$ a vanishing fraction of the mass of the positive part, with a power saving. For $\alpha\ge1$ no zero lies to the right of $\alpha$ and $m_\alpha^-=0$. Under the density hypothesis ($N(\sigma,T)\le T^{2(1-\sigma)+o(1)}$, where $N(\sigma,T)$ counts the zeros with $\beta\ge\sigma$ and $0<\gamma\le T$) the same bound holds with $e(\alpha)=2(1-\alpha)$. RH holds if and only if $v_\alpha^-$ vanishes identically for every $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$. The proof combines the zero density estimates of Ingham, of Guth and Maynard and of Huxley.
results.label: ag:thm:almost

results.name: Canonical factorisation of the shifted clock transform into a GGC and a defect
results.summary: The Laplace transform of the shifted clock factorises exactly as the transform of a GGC times an explicit defect that carries every zero to the right of the basepoint and equals one if and only if there is none.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$), counted with multiplicity, let $P_w(x)=w/(\pi(w^2+x^2))$ be the Cauchy kernel of width $w>0$, with $P_0$ the unit point mass at $0$, and for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ let $\varphi_\alpha(u)=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$ be the Laplace transform of the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ and $v_\alpha^+(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta+\gamma)]$ (a zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ contributes a unit atom at its ordinate). For every $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ and $u\ge0$, $\varphi_\alpha(u)=\varphi_\alpha^+(u)\,D_\alpha(u)$, where $\varphi_\alpha^+(u)=\exp\big\{-\int_0^\infty\log\big(1+u/\theta^2\big)\,\frac{v_\alpha^+(\theta)}{\pi}\,d\theta\big\}$ and $D_\alpha(u)=\prod_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}\frac{(\beta-\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}{(\sqrt{u}-\beta+\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}$. Here $\varphi_\alpha^+$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) $T_\alpha^+$ with Thorin density $v_\alpha^+/\pi$ in the chart $\theta=\sqrt{z}$, and the product defining the defect $D_\alpha$ runs over the zeros to the right of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ and converges absolutely. The defect is identically one if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$, and then $T_\alpha\overset{d}{=}T_\alpha^+$. Otherwise $D_\alpha(u)\to0$ as $u\to\infty$, and $T_\alpha^+$ is not the sum of $T_\alpha$ and an independent nonnegative variable.
results.label: ag:prop:factor

results.name: Explicit bounds on the defect from the verification of RH
results.summary: Using the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, with part of the proof certified in ball arithmetic, the defect of the shifted clock is within $e^{\pm1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}$ of one and the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $1.5\times10^{12}$ once the basepoint exceeds one half by more than $6\times10^{-10}$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$), counted with multiplicity, let $P_w(x)=w/(\pi(w^2+x^2))$ be the Cauchy kernel of width $w>0$, with $P_0$ the unit point mass at $0$, and for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ let $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)=v_\alpha^+(\theta)-v_\alpha^-(\theta)$ with $v_\alpha^+(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta+\gamma)]$ and $v_\alpha^-(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta+\gamma)]$. The shifted clock $T_\alpha$ has Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})=\varphi_\alpha^+(u)D_\alpha(u)$, where $\varphi_\alpha^+(u)=\exp\{-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/\theta^2)\,v_\alpha^+(\theta)\,\pi^{-1}d\theta\}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with Thorin density $v_\alpha^+/\pi$ and $D_\alpha(u)=\prod_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}\frac{(\beta-\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}{(\sqrt{u}-\beta+\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}$ is the defect. Let $T_0=3\times10^{12}$, below which all zeros lie on the critical line (the verification of Platt and Trudgian), and let $\Sigma_0=\sum_{\gamma>T_0}\gamma^{-2}$, the sum over all zeros above $T_0$ counted with multiplicity. By the Riemann von Mangoldt formula with the explicit error term of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, $\Sigma_0$ differs from $\frac{\log(T_0/2\pi)+1}{2\pi T_0}=1.4797\times10^{-12}$ by less than $2\times10^{-24}$, so $\Sigma_0<1.48\times10^{-12}$. Then for every $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ and every $u\ge0$: (1) $|\log D_\alpha(u)|\le(u+\sqrt{u})\,\Sigma_0$, so that $e^{-1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}\varphi_\alpha^+(u)\le\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}\le e^{1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}\varphi_\alpha^+(u)$; (2) the negative part of the density satisfies $v_\alpha^-(\theta)/\pi\le2\Sigma_0/\pi<9.43\times10^{-13}$ for $0\le\theta\le T_0/2$; (3) consequently $v_\alpha(\theta)>0$ for all $0\le\theta\le T_0/2$ whenever $\alpha-\frac{1}{2}>6\times10^{-10}$. Part of the proof is certified in ball arithmetic.
results.label: ag:thm:explicit

results.name: Positivity of the Thorin density on the verified window
results.summary: For every basepoint above one half the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $3\times10^{12}$ minus one half, and for basepoints up to $7.35$ it is smallest at the origin up to the height $3\times10^{12}-(1+\sqrt{2})/2$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, let $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)$ for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ (the function whose quotient by $\pi$ is the Thorin density of the shifted clock $T_\alpha$, the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$, in the chart $\theta=\sqrt{z}$, when every zero lies to the left of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$), let $T_0=3\times10^{12}$ (every zero off the critical line has $|\gamma|>T_0$, by the verification of Platt and Trudgian) and let $V_\xi=(\log\xi)''(\frac{1}{2})=0.04620998623$. (1) For every $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$, $v_\alpha(\theta)>0$ for $|\theta|\le T_0-\frac{1}{2}$. (2) For every $\alpha\in(\frac{1}{2},7.35]$, $v_\alpha(\theta)>v_\alpha(0)$ for $0<|\theta|\le T_0-\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}$, and $0<v_\alpha(0)\le(\alpha-\frac{1}{2})V_\xi$.
results.label: cor:dbeta:window

results.name: Size biased clock and the exponential mixture form of RH
results.summary: With no hypothesis the size biased clock is the clock plus an independent variable whose density is the heat trace divided by its integral, and RH holds exactly when that variable is a mixture of exponential laws (Steutel's decomposition applied to the clock).
results.statement:
Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)$, an entire function of $u$ whose zeros are the numbers $-a_k$, $a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2$, one for each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$ counted with multiplicity (so $a_k=\gamma_k^2>0$ for a zero $\rho_k=\tfrac12+i\gamma_k$ on the critical line). With no hypothesis $1/G$ is the Laplace transform of a probability law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$ for $u\ge0$. Let $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$, $t>0$, be the heat trace, let $m_0=\mathbb{E}T=\sum_ka_k^{-1}=0.0231049931\ldots$, and let $\widehat T$ be the size biased clock, the variable with law $t\,\mathbb{P}(T\in dt)/m_0$.
With no hypothesis, $\widehat T\overset{d}{=}T+A$, where $A$ is independent of $T$ and has density $W(t)/m_0$ on $(0,\infty)$. The Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if $A$ is a mixture of exponential laws, that is, $A\overset{d}{=}E/V$ with $E$ a standard exponential variable independent of a variable $V>0$; and then $V$ has the law $m_0^{-1}\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros $\tfrac12+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity.
results.label: pk:prop:sizebias

results.name: Centre clock lies in Urbanik class L2 and not in L3
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, and certified in ball arithmetic, the centre clock lies in Urbanik's class $L_2$ and not in $L_3$, because the third ladder function of the heat trace is positive while the fourth is negative at $e^{-4.15}$.
results.statement:
Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)$, an entire function of $u$ whose zeros are the numbers $-a_k$, $a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2$, one for each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$ counted with multiplicity. With no hypothesis $1/G$ is the Laplace transform of a probability law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ (the centre clock), and $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$, $t>0$, is the heat trace. The ladder functions are $W^{[0]}=W$ and $W^{[j+1]}(t)=-t\,\frac{d}{dt}W^{[j]}(t)$. With no hypothesis the clock is self decomposable: $T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t$ for a subordinator $Z=Z^{[1]}$, its driving process, with Laplace exponent $u(\log G)'(u)$ and Lévy density $-W'(x)$; and $Z^{[j+1]}$ denotes the driving process of the law of $Z^{[j]}_1$ whenever that law is self decomposable. A law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is self decomposable if for every $c\in(0,1)$ there is a law $\mu_c$ with $\widehat\mu(z)=\widehat\mu(cz)\widehat{\mu_c}(z)$ for the characteristic functions; Urbanik's class $L_0$ consists of the self decomposable laws and, for $n\ge1$, $L_n$ consists of the laws in $L_{n-1}$ all of whose components $\mu_c$ lie in $L_{n-1}$.
Unconditionally, that is, using only the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis below height $2197.3$ (Platt and Trudgian): $W^{[3]}(t)>0$ for every $t>0$, and $W^{[4]}(e^{-4.15})<0$ (in ball arithmetic $W^{[4]}(e^{-4.15})=-0.11089729616255\pm10^{-23}$). Consequently $W$, $W^{[1]}$ and $W^{[2]}$ are positive on $(0,\infty)$; the centre clock lies in $L_2$ and not in $L_3$; its driving process $Z=Z^{[1]}$ and the driving process $Z^{[2]}$ of $Z$ are self decomposable at every time (the laws of $Z_s$ and of $Z^{[2]}_s$ are self decomposable for every $s>0$); and the driving process $Z^{[3]}$ of $Z^{[2]}$ is self decomposable at no time.
results.label: pk:thm:ladder

results.name: First two driving processes of the clock are self decomposable and unimodal
results.summary: With no hypothesis, at every time the laws of the driving process of the clock and of the driving process of that process are self decomposable, hence unimodal, and the first lies in Urbanik's class $L_1$.
results.statement:
Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)$, and $T$ the clock, the random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$ for $u\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis). With no hypothesis $T$ is self decomposable: $T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t$ for a subordinator $Z$, its driving process, with Laplace exponent $u(\log G)'(u)$; and $Z^{[2]}$ denotes the driving process of the self decomposable law of $Z_1$. A law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is self decomposable if for every $c\in(0,1)$ there is a law $\mu_c$ with $\widehat\mu(z)=\widehat\mu(cz)\widehat{\mu_c}(z)$ for the characteristic functions; Urbanik's class $L_1$ consists of the self decomposable laws all of whose components $\mu_c$ are self decomposable.
